vocabulary.translation: 剧烈运动时心率会加快。

vocabulary.entry: blood pressure /blʌd ˈpreʃə(r)/ n. 血压
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise can help keep your blood pressure under control.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动有助于控制血压。

vocabulary.entry: reduce the chance of injury /rɪˈdjuːs ðə tʃɑːns ɒv ˈɪndʒəri/ 降低受伤几率；减少受伤可能性
vocabulary.example: Stretching before exercise can reduce the chance of injury.
vocabulary.translation: 运动前拉伸可以降低受伤几率。

vocabulary.entry: improve performance /ɪmˈpruːv pəˈfɔːməns/ 提升表现；改善运动成绩
vocabulary.example: Regular training is the key to improving athletic performance.
vocabulary.translation: 规律训练是提升运动表现的关键。

vocabulary.entry: ultimately /ˈʌltɪmətli/ adv. 最终；归根结底；最后
vocabulary.example: Ultimately, success depends on hard work and persistence.
vocabulary.translation: 成功归根结底取决于努力和坚持。

sentences.english: With our already busy lives, finding time to exercise can feel like one more thing on our ‘to do’ list.
sentences.chinese: 在本就忙碌的生活里，挤出时间运动仿佛成了待办清单上又一项负担。

sentences.english: So maybe it would help if there was ‘a best time’ to exercise?
sentences.chinese: 那么，如果存在一个“最佳运动时间”，会不会让这件事变得更容易？

sentences.english: Could exercising at certain times help maximise our fitness goals?
sentences.chinese: 在特定时间运动，能否帮助我们更高效地达成健身目标？

sentences.english: The answer is ‘yes’, but it’s easier than you think – no matter who you are, or when you like to work out.
sentences.chinese: 答案是肯定的，但这件事比你想象的要简单——无论你是谁，无论你喜欢在什么时段锻炼。

sentences.english: There are clear benefits to exercising in the morning.
sentences.chinese: 早上运动有着显而易见的好处。

sentences.english: Many of us have more free time compared to later in the day, and it may therefore be easier for us to stick to a morning workout routine.
sentences.chinese: 相比一天中的其他时段，我们很多人早上的空闲时间更多，因此也更容易坚持晨练的习惯。

sentences.english: A study published in Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise found that participants who exercised in the morning, increased their physical activity throughout the day, were less distracted by food, and slept better.
sentences.chinese: 一项发表在《运动医学与科学》期刊上的研究发现，早上运动的参与者，在一天当中的身体活动量会有所增加，对食物的注意力会降低，睡眠质量也会更好。

sentences.english: Exercising on an empty stomach before breakfast could also burn more fat and increase metabolism, which means you’ll continue to burn calories throughout the day.
sentences.chinese: 早餐前空腹运动，还能燃烧更多脂肪并提升新陈代谢，这意味着你在一整天里都会持续消耗卡路里。

sentences.english: So, good news for early birds, but what if you’re not a morning person?
sentences.chinese: 所以这对早起的人来说是个好消息，但如果你不习惯早起该怎么办呢？

sentences.english: Working out in the afternoon or evening also has benefits, just different ones.
sentences.chinese: 下午或晚上运动有与上午运动不同的好处。

sentences.english: For example, your body’s ability to perform peaks in the afternoon, according to a 2010 study by the Scandinavian Journal of Medicine and Science in Sports.
sentences.chinese: 例如，据《斯堪的纳维亚运动医学与科学期刊》2010年的一项研究显示，人体的运动表现能力在下午会达到峰值。

sentences.english: Also, in the afternoon and evening, your reaction time is quickest, and your heart rate and blood pressure are lowest, which reduce your chance of injury while improving performance.
sentences.chinese: 此外，在下午和晚上，人的反应速度最快，心率和血压也处于最低水平，这既能降低受伤风险，又能提升运动表现。

sentences.english: But does any of this change depending on whether you’re a man or a woman?
sentences.chinese: 但这些结论会因性别不同而有所变化吗？

sentences.english: Our bodies are different, after all, so the best time to exercise may be different too.
sentences.chinese: 毕竟男女的身体结构存在差异，那么运动的最佳时间或许也不尽相同。

sentences.english: A 2022 study from Skidmore College, New York, looked at exactly this question and the results showed that there are some differences.
sentences.chinese: 纽约斯基德莫尔学院2022年的一项研究就针对这个问题展开了调查，结果显示确实存在一些差异。

sentences.english: Want to reduce your blood pressure and you’re a woman? Exercise in the morning. Want to improve your heart health and you’re a man? Evening is better for you.
sentences.chinese: 如果你是女性，想要降低血压，那就选择早上运动；如果你是男性，想要改善心脏健康，晚上运动则更适合你。

sentences.english: But, ultimately, the study found that there are clear benefits for both sexes to exercising at either time of day.
sentences.chinese: 不过该研究最终也指出，无论男女，在一天中的任意时段运动，都能收获显著的益处。

sentences.english: So what time is best?
sentences.chinese: 那么到底什么时间运动最好呢？

sentences.english: It seems the answer is: whatever time is best for you!
sentences.chinese: 答案似乎是：最适合你的时间，就是最佳时间！

title: Finding your doppelganger
titleChinese: 寻找长相酷似你的那个人
paragraphs: What is the likelihood of you having someone who looks just like you? Would it be a good thing? And if you did have one, would you want to meet them?

Consider how often your facial features are used to identify you. Your passport, ID card and driving licence all bare your face. To enter your workplace, you likely need to be recognisable. You may need your face to unlock your smartphone and possibly even need it to exclude you from being present at a crime scene.

The word ‘doppelganger’ refers to a person who looks the same as you, essentially sharing your features; those that you thought were unique to you and your identity. Not an identical twin, as a doppelganger has no relation to you. The idea originated in German folklore. A doppelganger was said to be a spirit-double that replicated every human and beast on earth.

So, let’s get real. What are the chances of you having one in the first place? There’s said to be a one in 135 chance of an absolute dead ringer for you existing anywhere in the world, so the chances are pretty low, despite folk wisdom promising you otherwise. And the chances of meeting? The mathematical certainty of finding this particular person is supposedly less than one in a trillion!

That said, these statistics may be a good thing. Historically, having a double hasn’t always been a positive. Back in 1999, an innocent American man, indistinguishable from the real criminal, was sent to prison for robbery, where he stayed for 19 years. In the end, it turned out to be a case of mistaken identity. In a different case, a woman in New York was accused of trying to poison her doppelganger with deadly cheesecake so that she could steal her identity!

And, why are people interested in finding their possible doppelganger anyway? It may be helpful to look to the past when facial resemblance indicated kinship. Maybe one day you’ll meet your lookalike, but we understand that, after this, you possibly don’t want to!

vocabulary.entry: likelihood /ˈlaɪklihʊd/ n. 可能性；可能发生的事
vocabulary.example: There is a high likelihood of rain later today.
vocabulary.translation: 今天晚些时候下雨的可能性很大。

vocabulary.entry: crime scene /ˈkraɪm siːn/ n. 犯罪现场

vocabulary.entry: doppelganger /ˈdɒpəlɡæŋə(r)/ n. 面貌酷似的人；分身（词源为德语）

sentences.chinese: 还有另一个案例，纽约一名女子被指控试图用有毒的芝士蛋糕毒害自己的分身，目的竟是为了窃取对方的身份！

sentences.chinese: 那么，人们为什么会对寻找自己可能存在的分身感兴趣呢？

sentences.english: It may be helpful to look to the past when facial resemblance indicated kinship.
sentences.chinese: 或许我们可以回溯到过去——在那个年代，面容相似往往意味着血缘关系。

title: Second-hand clothes and reducing your fashion footprint
paragraphs: The destructive impact of fast fashion on the environment is widely documented. So how can we, as consumers, reduce our fashion footprint? One obvious answer is to buy less. Another is to buy clothes that have been more sustainably made, using organic and recycled materials. Hiring clothes is another way to get new pieces for our wardrobe. But buying second-hand may be the simplest solution and a trend that is growing fast.

According to the Boston Consulting Group, second-hand clothes are projected to make up 27 per cent of customers’ wardrobes by 2023. By 2030, the second-hand clothing market is projected to be twice the size of fast fashion, according to a global report by Thredup and GlobalData. So, it seems, the next ten years will see the resale market grow fast, and this is in part because we now have more options than simply buying from charity shops and jumble sales. Online sites are making it easier to both buy and sell pre-loved items.

It also helps that the perception of pre-loved clothing has changed. Dr Amna Khan, senior lecturer in consumer behaviours and retail at Manchester Metropolitan University, said ‘it’s now become trendy to wear second-hand’ and it’s no longer ‘a case of only buying it if you can’t afford anything else’. The changing values of shoppers is even being seen in celebrity culture, with television personalities, such as contestants on the popular UK TV show Love Island, promoting second-hand clothing.

Not everyone is convinced that these changes in shopping habits will do enough to reduce our fashion footprint. The charity Wrap tells people to repair and revamp clothes they already have in their wardrobe before buying new ones, even if they are second-hand. But it’s clear that some consumers now want to consume less and make more environmentally friendly choices when they do buy. The fashion industry is therefore having to change, and the second-hand market is the star of the show.

vocabulary.entry: destructive /dɪˈstrʌktɪv/ adj. 破坏性的；造成严重损害的
vocabulary.example: The storm had a destructive effect on the coastal village.
vocabulary.translation: 这场风暴对这个沿海村庄造成了毁灭性的影响。

vocabulary.entry: fast fashion /ˌfɑːst ˈfæʃn/ n. 快时尚（指快速推出新款、追求高销量的时尚产业模式）
vocabulary.example: Fast fashion has been criticized for its negative environmental impact.
vocabulary.translation: 快时尚因其对环境的负面影响而受到批评。

vocabulary.entry: fashion footprint /ˈfæʃn ˈfʊtprɪnt/ n. 时尚碳足迹；时尚消费行为对环境产生的整体影响
vocabulary.example: We all need to reduce our fashion footprint by making more sustainable choices.
vocabulary.translation: 我们都需要通过做出更可持续的选择来减少自己的时尚碳足迹。

vocabulary.entry: sustainably /səˈsteɪnəbli/ adv. 可持续地；符合生态可持续发展原则地
vocabulary.example: The company is committed to producing clothes more sustainably.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司致力于更可持续地生产服装。

vocabulary.entry: organic /ɔːˈɡænɪk/ adj. 有机的（指原料未使用人工化肥、农药等化学物质的）
vocabulary.example: This shirt is made from organic cotton grown without pesticides.
vocabulary.translation: 这件衬衫由未使用农药种植的有机棉制成。

vocabulary.entry: recycled materials /rɪˈsaɪkld məˈtɪəriəlz/ n. 再生材料；回收利用的原材料
vocabulary.example: The brand uses recycled materials to make its bags and accessories.
vocabulary.translation: 这个品牌使用再生材料制作包袋和配饰。

vocabulary.entry: hire /ˈhaɪə(r)/ v. 租用；租借（衣物、饰品等）
vocabulary.example: She decided to hire a dress for the wedding instead of buying one.
vocabulary.translation: 她决定为婚礼租一条裙子，而不是买一条。

vocabulary.entry: second-hand /ˌsekənd ˈhænd/ adj. 二手的；用过的
vocabulary.example: I bought a second-hand jacket in excellent condition from an online shop.
vocabulary.translation: 我从一家网店买了一件成色极好的二手夹克。

vocabulary.entry: project /prəˈdʒekt/ v. 预测；预计；推算（未来趋势、数据等）
vocabulary.example: Sales are projected to rise by 10% next year.
vocabulary.translation: 预计明年的销售额将增长10%。

vocabulary.entry: resale market /ˈriːseɪl ˈmɑːkɪt/ n. 转售市场；二手交易市场
vocabulary.example: The resale market for luxury bags has grown rapidly in recent years.
vocabulary.translation: 奢侈品包的二手转售市场近年来发展迅速。

vocabulary.entry: in part /ɪn pɑːt/ 部分地；在某种程度上
vocabulary.example: The success of the project is in part due to the team's hard work.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目的成功在一定程度上归功于团队的努力。

vocabulary.entry: charity shop /ˈtʃærəti ʃɒp/ n. 慈善商店（售卖捐赠物品，所得款项用于慈善事业）
vocabulary.example: I often find nice clothes at the charity shop near my home.
vocabulary.translation: 我经常在我家附近的慈善商店淘到好看的衣服。

vocabulary.entry: jumble sale /ˈdʒʌmbl seɪl/ n. 旧货义卖；杂物拍卖会（多为慈善性质，售卖各类捐赠旧货）
vocabulary.example: The local church holds a jumble sale every spring to raise money for charity.
vocabulary.translation: 当地的教堂每年春天都会举办旧货义卖，为慈善事业筹款。

vocabulary.entry: pre-loved /ˌpriː ˈlʌvd/ adj. 二手的；被爱过的（委婉说法，时尚领域常用，指经他人使用但仍有价值的）
vocabulary.example: The online platform specializes in selling pre-loved designer clothing.
vocabulary.translation: 这个线上平台专门售卖二手的设计师服装。

vocabulary.entry: perception /pəˈsepʃn/ n. 看法；认知；大众观念
vocabulary.example: Public perception of the brand has improved since the new campaign.
vocabulary.translation: 自新的宣传活动开展后，大众对这个品牌的印象有所改观。

vocabulary.entry: consumer behaviour /kənˈsjuːmə bɪˈheɪvjə(r)/ n. 消费者行为（指消费者在购买、使用、处置商品过程中的一系列行为）
vocabulary.example: The course covers topics such as consumer behaviour and marketing strategies.
vocabulary.translation: 这门课程涵盖消费者行为和营销策略等主题。

vocabulary.entry: retail /ˈriːteɪl/ n. 零售；零售业
vocabulary.example: He has worked in retail for over 20 years and knows the market well.
vocabulary.translation: 他在零售业工作了20多年，对市场十分了解。

vocabulary.entry: trendy /ˈtrendi/ adj. 时髦的；流行的；赶潮流的
vocabulary.example: Wearing vintage jeans is very trendy among young people now.
vocabulary.translation: 穿复古牛仔裤现在在年轻人中非常流行。

vocabulary.entry: a case of /ə keɪs ɒv/ 一种……的情况；属于……情形
vocabulary.example: It's not a case of being lazy—he just doesn't have enough time.
vocabulary.translation: 这不是懒的问题，他只是没有足够的时间。

vocabulary.entry: afford /əˈfɔːd/ v. 买得起；负担得起（时间、金钱、精力等）
vocabulary.example: I can't afford to buy a new car right now.
vocabulary.translation: 我现在买不起新车。

vocabulary.entry: celebrity culture /səˈlebrəti ˈkʌltʃə(r)/ n. 名人文化；明星文化（受明星言行、喜好影响的社会文化现象）
vocabulary.example: Celebrity culture has a huge influence on young people's fashion choices.
vocabulary.translation: 名人文化对年轻人的时尚选择有着巨大的影响。

vocabulary.entry: television personality /ˈtelɪvɪʒn ˌpɜːsəˈnæləti/ n. 电视名人；电视明星（因电视节目走红的公众人物）
vocabulary.example: She started as a television personality and later became a successful actress.
vocabulary.translation: 她最初是一名电视名人，后来成为了一名成功的演员。

vocabulary.entry: contestant /kənˈtestənt/ n. 参赛者；竞争者（比赛、选秀节目等的）
vocabulary.example: The contestant won the first prize in the singing competition.
vocabulary.translation: 这位参赛者在歌唱比赛中获得了一等奖。

vocabulary.entry: promote /prəˈməʊt/ v. 推广；宣传；提倡（理念、产品、行为等）
vocabulary.example: The government is trying to promote sustainable living among citizens.
vocabulary.translation: 政府正努力在市民中推广可持续的生活方式。

vocabulary.entry: convince /kənˈvɪns/ v. 使信服；使确信；说服
vocabulary.example: I can't convince him to change his mind about the plan.
vocabulary.translation: 我无法说服他改变对这个计划的想法。

vocabulary.entry: shopping habit /ˈʃɒpɪŋ ˈhæbɪt/ n. 购物习惯
vocabulary.example: Changing your shopping habits can help you save money and reduce waste.
vocabulary.translation: 改变购物习惯能帮你省钱并减少浪费。

vocabulary.entry: revamp /riˈvæmp/ v. 翻新；改造；重新设计（衣物、形象、产品等）
vocabulary.example: She decided to revamp her old dress by adding some lace and buttons.
vocabulary.translation: 她决定给旧裙子加些蕾丝和纽扣，把它翻新一下。

vocabulary.entry: environmentally friendly /ɪnˌvaɪrənˈmentəli ˈfrendli/ adj. 环保的；对环境无害的
vocabulary.example: This brand only uses environmentally friendly packaging for its products.
vocabulary.translation: 这个品牌的产品只使用环保包装。

vocabulary.entry: fashion industry /ˈfæʃn ˈɪndəstri/ n. 时尚产业；服装行业
vocabulary.example: The fashion industry is constantly changing with new trends every season.
vocabulary.translation: 时尚产业变化不断，每个季节都有新的潮流。

vocabulary.entry: star of the show /stɑː(r) ɒv ðə ʃəʊ/ 焦点；核心；主角（口语）
vocabulary.example: The new smartphone was the star of the show at the tech exhibition.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新手机是此次科技展的焦点。

sentences.english: The destructive impact of fast fashion on the environment is widely documented.
sentences.chinese: 快时尚对环境造成的破坏性影响已被大量研究证实。

sentences.english: So how can we, as consumers, reduce our fashion footprint?
sentences.chinese: 那么，作为消费者，我们该如何减少自己的时尚碳足迹呢？

sentences.english: One obvious answer is to buy less.
sentences.chinese: 一个显而易见的办法是减少购买量。

sentences.english: Another is to buy clothes that have been more sustainably made, using organic and recycled materials.
sentences.chinese: 另一个办法是选购采用有机及再生材料制作、更具可持续性的服装。

sentences.english: Hiring clothes is another way to get new pieces for our wardrobe.
sentences.chinese: 租衣服也是为衣橱添置新品的一种方式。

sentences.english: But buying second-hand may be the simplest solution and a trend that is growing fast.
sentences.chinese: 但购买二手衣物或许是最简单的解决方案，同时这也是一个正在迅速兴起的趋势。

sentences.english: According to the Boston Consulting Group, second-hand clothes are projected to make up 27 per cent of customers’ wardrobes by 2023.
sentences.chinese: 波士顿咨询集团的数据显示，到2023年，二手衣物预计将占到消费者衣橱衣物总量的27%。

sentences.english: By 2030, the second-hand clothing market is projected to be twice the size of fast fashion, according to a global report by Thredup and GlobalData.
sentences.chinese: 二手寄售平台Thredup与市场研究机构GlobalData联合发布的一份全球报告指出，到2030年，二手服装市场的规模预计将达到快时尚市场的两倍。

sentences.english: So, it seems, the next ten years will see the resale market grow fast, and this is in part because we now have more options than simply buying from charity shops and jumble sales. Online sites are making it easier to both buy and sell pre-loved items.
sentences.chinese: 由此可见，貌似未来十年二手转售市场将迎来快速增长，部分原因在于，如今人们购买二手衣物的渠道不再局限于慈善商店和旧货义卖活动，各类线上平台让二手物品的买卖变得愈发便捷。

sentences.english: It also helps that the perception of pre-loved clothing has changed.
sentences.chinese: 公众对二手衣物的看法转变也推动了这一趋势的发展。

sentences.english: Dr Amna Khan, senior lecturer in consumer behaviours and retail at Manchester Metropolitan University, said ‘it’s now become trendy to wear second-hand’ and it’s no longer ‘a case of only buying it if you can’t afford anything else’.
sentences.chinese: 曼彻斯特城市大学消费者行为与零售业高级讲师阿姆娜·汗博士表示，“如今穿二手衣已经成了一种潮流”，而不再是“只有买不起新衣服才会去买的无奈之选”。

sentences.english: The changing values of shoppers is even being seen in celebrity culture, with television personalities, such as contestants on the popular UK TV show Love Island, promoting second-hand clothing.
sentences.chinese: 消费者的价值观转变甚至在名人文化中也有所体现，英国热门电视节目《爱情岛》的选手等电视名人都在为二手服装代言宣传。

sentences.english: Not everyone is convinced that these changes in shopping habits will do enough to reduce our fashion footprint.
sentences.chinese: 不过，并非所有人都认为购物习惯的这些转变足以减少我们的时尚碳足迹。

sentences.english: The charity Wrap tells people to repair and revamp clothes they already have in their wardrobe before buying new ones, even if they are second-hand.
sentences.chinese: 慈善机构WRAP建议人们，在购买新衣服（即便是二手衣物）之前，先对衣橱里现有的衣服进行修补和翻新。

sentences.english: But it’s clear that some consumers now want to consume less and make more environmentally friendly choices when they do buy.
sentences.chinese: 但显而易见的是，如今部分消费者希望减少消费，并且在不得不购买时做出更环保的选择。

sentences.english: The fashion industry is therefore having to change, and the second-hand market is the star of the show.
sentences.chinese: 时尚行业因此不得不做出改变，而二手市场则成了这场变革中的主角。

title: Why do we dream
paragraphs: There are no clear answers to the question of why we dream, but there are different theories. Dreaming is extraordinary and strange: you hallucinate, believe impossible things, and people you know may merge into one another. And then, to top it off, you will likely forget all about it.

Memory storage could be one reason for why we dream. When you are asleep, the brain decides what information you should move to your long-term memory and what should be unlearnt. In a TED Talk, psychologist Amy Adkins described a 2010 experiment involving participants studying how to get out of a complex 3D maze. It was found that they were much better at attempting it if they had had a nap and dreamt of the maze.

Another purpose of dreams could be the processing of our daily emotions, which may add to emotional memory consolidation. In 2003, the Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience published research that experimented with the idea of dreams being a replication of our daily lives. Diary entries and dream journals of 29 healthy young adults over a two-week period were compared, and it was discovered that emotional themes from the day were replicated in dreams 35-55% of the time.

Antti Revonsuo, a Finnish scientist, has suggested that dreaming helps us to prepare for and deal with stressful situations. He studied children’s nightmares, giving an example of being continuously chased by wolves. He believes dreams like this stem from our ancestors and could be a rehearsal for daily struggle and survival. In modern times, dreams and nightmares may be preparing us for social situations such as having a fight with a friend, going on a date or having a job interview.
With such a variety of theories on why we dream, it seems that more research is needed before we can completely understand their purpose.

vocabulary.entry: extraordinary /ɪkˈstrɔːdnri/ adj. 非同寻常的；奇异的；特别的
vocabulary.example: The view from the top of the mountain is simply extraordinary.
vocabulary.translation: 山顶的景色简直美极了，非同寻常。

vocabulary.entry: hallucinate /həˈluːsɪneɪt/ v. 产生幻觉；出现幻视、幻听等
vocabulary.example: People who are severely sleep-deprived may hallucinate.
vocabulary.translation: 严重睡眠不足的人可能会产生幻觉。

vocabulary.entry: merge into one another /mɜːdʒ ɪntu wʌn əˈnʌðə(r)/ 相互融合；合为一体
vocabulary.example: The colours of the sunset merged into one another on the horizon.
vocabulary.translation: 日落的各色霞光在地平线上相互交融。

vocabulary.entry: to top it off /tu tɒp ɪt ɒf/ （口语）更有甚者；除此之外还有；更糟的是
vocabulary.example: We lost our way, and to top it off, it started to pour with rain.
vocabulary.translation: 我们迷了路，更糟的是，天还下起了瓢泼大雨。

vocabulary.entry: memory storage /ˈmeməri ˈstɔːrɪdʒ/ n. 记忆存储
vocabulary.example: The brain has a complex system for memory storage and retrieval.
vocabulary.translation: 大脑拥有一套复杂的记忆存储与提取系统。

vocabulary.entry: long-term memory /ˌlɒŋ tɜːm ˈmeməri/ n. 长期记忆
vocabulary.example: Childhood memories are often stored in our long-term memory for decades.
vocabulary.translation: 童年的记忆往往会在我们的长期记忆中留存数十年。

vocabulary.entry: unlearnt /ʌnˈlɜːnt/ v. 忘却；摒弃（已学的知识、习惯等）
vocabulary.example: It takes time to unlearnt the bad habits formed in childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 摒弃童年养成的坏习惯需要时间。

vocabulary.entry: psychologist /saɪˈkɒlədʒɪst/ n. 心理学家
vocabulary.example: The psychologist gave her some advice on how to manage her anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 这位心理学家为她提供了一些应对焦虑的建议。

vocabulary.entry: complex 3D maze /ˈkɒmpleks θriː diː meɪz/ n. 复杂的三维迷宫
vocabulary.example: The game requires players to navigate a complex 3D maze to find the treasure.
vocabulary.translation: 这款游戏要求玩家穿越复杂的三维迷宫寻找宝藏。

vocabulary.entry: nap /næp/ n. 小睡；打盹 v. （短暂地）小睡，打盹
vocabulary.example: I usually take a short nap after lunch to boost my energy.
vocabulary.translation: 我通常午饭后小睡一会儿来恢复精力。

vocabulary.entry: processing of daily emotions /ˈprəʊsesɪŋ ɒv ˈdeɪli ɪˈməʊʃnz/ n. 日常情绪的处理
vocabulary.example: Sleep plays an important role in the processing of daily emotions.
vocabulary.translation: 睡眠在日常情绪的处理中起着重要作用。

vocabulary.entry: emotional memory consolidation /ɪˌməʊʃənl ˈmeməri kənˌsɒlɪˈdeɪʃn/ n. 情绪记忆巩固
vocabulary.example: Research shows that deep sleep promotes emotional memory consolidation.
vocabulary.translation: 研究表明，深度睡眠能促进情绪记忆的巩固。

vocabulary.entry: Cognitive Neuroscience /ˈkɒɡnətɪv ˌnjʊərəʊˈsaɪəns/ n. 认知神经科学
vocabulary.example: Cognitive Neuroscience is a cross-disciplinary subject combining psychology and neuroscience.
vocabulary.translation: 认知神经科学是一门融合了心理学和神经科学的交叉学科。

vocabulary.entry: replication /ˌreplɪˈkeɪʃn/ n. 再现；复制；复刻
vocabulary.example: The replication of real-life events in dreams is a common psychological phenomenon.
vocabulary.translation: 现实事件在梦境中的再现是一种常见的心理现象。

vocabulary.entry: diary entry /ˈdaɪəri ˈentri/ n. 日记条目；日记内容
vocabulary.example: Each diary entry recorded her feelings about the day's events.
vocabulary.translation: 每一条日记都记录了她对当日发生之事的感受。

vocabulary.entry: dream journal /driːm ˈdʒɜːnl/ n. 梦境日记；梦记
vocabulary.example: She keeps a dream journal by her bed to write down her dreams every morning.
vocabulary.translation: 她在床边放了一本梦境日记，每天早上记录自己的梦。

vocabulary.entry: emotional theme /ɪˌməʊʃənl θiːm/ n. 情绪主题
vocabulary.example: Anxiety was the main emotional theme in his dreams after the accident.
vocabulary.translation: 事故后，焦虑是他梦境中主要的情绪主题。

vocabulary.entry: Finnish /ˈfɪnɪʃ/ adj. 芬兰的；芬兰人的 n. 芬兰语；芬兰人
vocabulary.example: This Finnish scientist has made great contributions to sleep research.
vocabulary.translation: 这位芬兰科学家为睡眠研究做出了巨大贡献。

vocabulary.entry: stressful situation /ˈstresfl ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃn/ n. 压力情境；紧张局面
vocabulary.example: It's important to stay calm when facing a stressful situation.
vocabulary.translation: 面对压力情境时保持冷静至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: nightmare /ˈnaɪtmeə(r)/ n. 噩梦；梦魇；令人极其不快的事
vocabulary.example: He woke up screaming from a nightmare about being chased by a monster.
vocabulary.translation: 他从被怪兽追赶的噩梦中尖叫着醒来。

vocabulary.entry: stem from /stem frəm/ 源于；来自；起因于
vocabulary.example: Many of our fears stem from forgotten childhood experiences.
vocabulary.translation: 我们的许多恐惧都源于被遗忘的童年经历。

vocabulary.entry: ancestor /ˈænsestə(r)/ n. 祖先；先祖；先驱
vocabulary.example: Our human ancestors first lived in Africa millions of years ago.
vocabulary.translation: 我们的人类祖先数百万年前最初生活在非洲。

vocabulary.entry: rehearsal /rɪˈhɜːsl/ n. 排练；预演；模拟演练
vocabulary.example: The dream was like a rehearsal for the important speech she had to give.
vocabulary.translation: 这个梦就像为她即将发表的重要演讲进行的一次模拟演练。

vocabulary.entry: daily struggle /ˈdeɪli ˈstrʌɡl/ n. 日常的挣扎；日常的艰难处境
vocabulary.example: For many low-income families, making ends meet is a daily struggle.
vocabulary.translation: 对许多低收入家庭来说，勉强维持生计是一场日常的挣扎。

vocabulary.entry: survival /səˈvaɪvl/ n. 生存；存活；生存能力
vocabulary.example: These skills were essential for the survival of early humans in harsh environments.
vocabulary.translation: 这些技能对早期人类在恶劣环境中的生存至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: social situation /ˈsəʊʃl ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃn/ n. 社交场景；社会情境
vocabulary.example: Children learn to behave properly in different social situations as they grow up.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子们在成长过程中学会在不同的社交场景中恰当表现。

vocabulary.entry: job interview /dʒɒb ˈɪntəvjuː/ n. 求职面试；工作面试
vocabulary.example: She spent hours preparing for the job interview with the big company.
vocabulary.translation: 她花了数小时为这家大公司的求职面试做准备。

sentences.english: There are no clear answers to the question of why we dream, but there are different theories.
sentences.chinese: 关于人为什么会做梦，目前尚无定论，但学界存在多种理论。

sentences.english: Dreaming is extraordinary and strange: you hallucinate, believe impossible things, and people you know may merge into one another.
sentences.chinese: 梦境离奇而玄妙：你会产生幻觉，相信一些不可能发生的事，认识的人会与梦境融为一体。

sentences.english: And then, to top it off, you will likely forget all about it.
sentences.chinese: 除此之外，醒来后你很可能会将这一切忘得一干二净。

sentences.english: Memory storage could be one reason for why we dream.
sentences.chinese: 记忆储存可能是做梦的原因之一。

sentences.chinese: 人处于睡眠状态时，大脑会筛选信息，决定哪些内容要转入长期记忆，哪些内容可以被遗忘。

sentences.english: In a TED Talk, psychologist Amy Adkins described a 2010 experiment involving participants studying how to get out of a complex 3D maze. It was found that they were much better at attempting it if they had had a nap and dreamt of the maze.
sentences.chinese: 心理学家埃米·阿德金斯在一场TED演讲中提到了2010年的一项实验：研究人员让参与者学习如何走出一个复杂的三维迷宫，结果发现，那些小憩时梦到迷宫的人，再次尝试走迷宫时表现要出色得多。

sentences.english: Another purpose of dreams could be the processing of our daily emotions, which may add to emotional memory consolidation.
sentences.chinese: 做梦的另一个作用可能是处理日常情绪，这有助于情绪记忆的巩固。

sentences.english: In 2003, the Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience published research that experimented with the idea of dreams being a replication of our daily lives.
sentences.chinese: 2003年，《认知神经科学杂志》刊登了一项研究，旨在验证“梦境是日常生活复现”这一观点。

sentences.english: Diary entries and dream journals of 29 healthy young adults over a two-week period were compared, and it was discovered that emotional themes from the day were replicated in dreams 35-55% of the time.
sentences.chinese: 研究人员对比了29名健康年轻人两周内的日记与梦境记录，发现日间的情绪主题在梦境中复现的概率为35%至55%。

sentences.english: Antti Revonsuo, a Finnish scientist, has suggested that dreaming helps us to prepare for and deal with stressful situations.
sentences.chinese: 芬兰科学家安蒂·雷翁苏奥提出，做梦能帮助我们为应对压力情境做好准备。

sentences.english: He studied children’s nightmares, giving an example of being continuously chased by wolves.
sentences.chinese: 他研究了儿童的噩梦，比如梦到被狼群持续追赶的场景。

sentences.english: He believes dreams like this stem from our ancestors and could be a rehearsal for daily struggle and survival.
sentences.chinese: 他认为这类梦境源于人类的祖先，是对日常生存斗争的预演。

sentences.english: In modern times, dreams and nightmares may be preparing us for social situations such as having a fight with a friend, going on a date or having a job interview.
sentences.chinese: 在现代社会，梦境（包括噩梦）则可能是在帮我们预演各类社交场景，比如和朋友吵架、约会或是参加求职面试。

sentences.english: With such a variety of theories on why we dream, it seems that more research is needed before we can completely understand their purpose.
sentences.chinese: 关于人为什么会做梦，理论层出不穷。貌似要想彻底弄清梦境的意义，我们还需要开展更多的研究。

title: Tips on saving energy
paragraphs: We all want to save money, and with the cost of living on the rise in the UK, it’s become more important than ever to watch what we spend. The biggest increase in our expenditure at the moment is on energy – the oil, gas and electricity we use to power and heat our homes. That’s why many of us are looking at ways to save energy so we don’t have to shell out on huge fuel bills.

Making our home more energy efficient is the obvious way to save money. To try to achieve this, new homes in the UK will be banned from installing new gas and oil boilers by 2025. Having a heat pump instead can help save energy, but they’re unaffordable for many people, unless they’ve got spare cash stashed away.

If your home feels like a money pit, there are some low-budget solutions you can turn to to lower your energy usage. Warm air escapes our homes easily, so adding draught excluders or a rolled-up towel to block these gaps will help. Investing in new double glazing will certainly insulate your home better, but if it is too costly, it might be worth using some heavy curtains to stop the heat escaping. Switching off lights is also a good idea.

But there are lots of other little things we can do around the home that will help save energy, don’t cost a fortune and that just require tweaks to our behaviour. They could be as good as installing, fitting or making anything. Put lids on pots and pans when cooking – the food will be ready quicker. Use a microwave to reheat food rather than the oven. Don’t overfill your kettle when boiling water, and don’t leave electrical items on standby. Jo Patterson from Cardiff University’s Welsh School of Architecture told the BBC that a combination of small measures like these could reduce household energy bills by about 10%.
So, we’re being encouraged to be more fuel efficient. But our main aim isn’t just financial – we need to do it to reduce our carbon footprint, so that our energy usage doesn’t cost the Earth.

vocabulary.entry: cost of living /ˌkɒst ɒv ˈlɪvɪŋ/ n. 生活成本
vocabulary.example: The cost of living in the capital has risen by 5% this year.
vocabulary.translation: 首都的生活成本今年上涨了5%。

vocabulary.entry: watch what we spend /wɒtʃ wɒt wi spend/ 精打细算；留意日常开支
vocabulary.example: We have to watch what we spend now that prices are going up everywhere.
vocabulary.translation: 现在各处物价都在涨，我们必须精打细算。

vocabulary.entry: expenditure /ɪkˈspendɪtʃə(r)/ n. 开支；消费；支出

vocabulary.translation: 我们需要削减非必要开支。

vocabulary.translation: 我不得不花500多英镑修我的车。

vocabulary.entry: fuel bill /ˈfjuːəl bɪl/ n. 能源账单；燃料费用单

vocabulary.entry: energy efficient /ˌenədʒi ɪˈfɪʃnt/ adj. 节能的；能源效率高的

vocabulary.entry: gas and oil boiler /ˌɡæs ənd ɔɪl ˈbɔɪlə(r)/ n. 燃气燃油锅炉

vocabulary.translation: 我们正把老式的燃气燃油锅炉换成更环保的系统。

vocabulary.translation: 热泵能高效地为房屋供暖和制冷。

vocabulary.entry: spare cash /speə kæʃ/ n. 闲钱；备用现金

vocabulary.translation: 今年我没有闲钱去度假。

vocabulary.entry: stash away /stæʃ əˈweɪ/ 储存；藏匿（钱财、物品）

vocabulary.translation: 她每个月都存一点钱以备不时之需。

vocabulary.entry: money pit /ˈmʌni pɪt/ n. （口语）烧钱的地方；持续耗费钱财的事物
vocabulary.example: This old house is a real money pit—we’re always paying for repairs.
vocabulary.translation: 这栋老房子就是个烧钱的坑，我们总在花钱修。

vocabulary.entry: low-budget /ˌləʊ ˈbʌdʒɪt/ adj. 低成本的；预算紧张的

vocabulary.translation: 我们想出了一个低成本的办法来解决这个问题。

vocabulary.translation: 这个应用会实时追踪你家的能源消耗情况。

vocabulary.translation: 我们决定买一台新的节能洗衣机。

vocabulary.entry: double glazing /ˌdʌbl ˈɡleɪzɪŋ/ n. 双层玻璃

vocabulary.translation: 我们需要给墙壁做保温处理来减少热量流失。

vocabulary.translation: 翻新整栋房子会花一大笔钱。

vocabulary.translation: 对计划做几处小调整就会使其变得完美。

vocabulary.translation: 饮食和运动相结合是减肥的最佳方式。

vocabulary.translation: 看到家庭能源账单金额下降，我们很开心。

title: How the Romans influenced English
titleChinese: 罗马文明对英语语言的影响
paragraphs: The Romans lived in Britain between 43AD and 410AD but their legacy is still felt today and not just in physical ruins. The Romans left us language, including some common English words.

During the Roman Empire, Latin, an ancient language, was spoken in many parts of Britain. While the Romans wrote in classical Latin, they conversed in vulgar Latin – colloquial, everyday language that was used between soldiers and in trade. Because of trade, words that stuck often relate to food and drink, such as ‘wine’, which came from the Latin ‘vinum’. Others relate to dwellings such as ‘kitchen’, derived from the verb ‘cook’, and ‘wall’, which originally referred to a stake or post outside a fort.

Settlements and roads in Roman times were extensive. The word ‘street’, used generally as well as being used for specific names of streets, originally came from ‘strata’ which meant paved road. On a similar note, academic research from the field of linguistics indicates many well-known place names in the UK owe their origin to Latin. For example, the Romans used ‘castrum’ to refer to a city, which developed into the common place ending -chester, -caster or -cester. Consider Manchester. It is a former Roman fort which was known as Mamuciam. Other places with Roman derivations include Lancaster and Leicester.

A significant impact on English which came from the Romans is the use of the Roman alphabet. Manuscripts of Old English texts have shown a version not unalike written English today. Differences include some letters however, such as two symbols called ‘ash’ and ‘eth’. Nowadays you are more likely to see these symbols in a guide to pronunciation.
So, even though 1,600 years have passed, the Romans live on.

vocabulary.entry: legacy /ˈleɡəsi/ n. 遗产；遗留的影响；传世之物
vocabulary.example: The artist left a lasting legacy of great paintings.
vocabulary.translation: 这位艺术家留下了一大批伟大的画作，成为不朽的遗产。

vocabulary.entry: physical /ˈfɪzɪkl/ adj. 有形的；物质的；实体的
vocabulary.example: The museum has a collection of physical relics from the ancient kingdom.
vocabulary.translation: 这家博物馆收藏了该古国的一批有形文物。

vocabulary.entry: ruin /ˈruːɪn/ n. 废墟；遗迹（复数ruins）
vocabulary.example: We visited the ancient ruins of the Roman city near the coast.
vocabulary.translation: 我们参观了海岸附近这座罗马古城的遗迹。

vocabulary.entry: Empire /ˈempaɪə(r)/ n. 帝国；（某领域的）统治地位
vocabulary.example: The Roman Empire once covered a large part of Europe.
vocabulary.translation: 罗马帝国曾占据欧洲的大部分地区。

vocabulary.entry: Latin /ˈlætn/ n. 拉丁语 adj. 拉丁语的；罗马的
vocabulary.example: Many English words have their roots in Latin.
vocabulary.translation: 许多英语单词都源于拉丁语。

vocabulary.entry: ancient /ˈeɪnʃənt/ adj. 古代的；古老的；年代久远的
vocabulary.example: This stone circle is an ancient monument dating back to 3000 BC.
vocabulary.translation: 这座石环是可追溯至公元前3000年的古老遗迹。

vocabulary.entry: classical /ˈklæsɪkl/ adj. 经典的；古典的；（语言）规范的
vocabulary.example: He studied classical Latin and Greek at university.
vocabulary.translation: 他在大学里学过古典拉丁语和希腊语。

vocabulary.entry: converse /kənˈvɜːs/ v. 交谈；谈话
vocabulary.example: They conversed for hours about their experiences abroad.
vocabulary.translation: 他们聊了几个小时各自在国外的经历。

vocabulary.entry: vulgar /ˈvʌlɡə(r)/ adj. 通俗的；民间的；粗俗的
vocabulary.example: Vulgar Latin was the everyday language spoken by ordinary Romans.
vocabulary.translation: 通俗拉丁语是古罗马平民使用的日常语言。

vocabulary.entry: colloquial /kəˈləʊkwiəl/ adj. 口语的；会话的；通俗的
vocabulary.example: The book uses colloquial English that is easy to understand.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书使用通俗易懂的英语口语表达。

vocabulary.entry: trade /treɪd/ n. 贸易；商业；交易 v. 做买卖；贸易
vocabulary.example: Trade between the two countries has increased greatly in recent years.
vocabulary.translation: 两国间的贸易近年来大幅增长。

vocabulary.entry: dwelling /ˈdwelɪŋ/ n. 住所；住宅；寓所
vocabulary.example: The old village has a variety of traditional stone dwellings.
vocabulary.translation: 这个古老的村庄有各式各样的传统石砌住宅。

vocabulary.entry: derive /dɪˈraɪv/ v. 源自；获得；推导出
vocabulary.example: This word is derived from a Greek verb meaning 'to write'.
vocabulary.translation: 这个单词源自古希腊的一个动词，意思是“书写”。

vocabulary.entry: verb /vɜːb/ n. 动词
vocabulary.example: In this sentence, 'run' is a transitive verb.
vocabulary.translation: 在这个句子中，“run”是及物动词。

vocabulary.entry: stake /steɪk/ n. 木桩；桩子；赌注 v. 以……打赌
vocabulary.example: They drove wooden stakes into the ground to mark the boundary.
vocabulary.translation: 他们把木桩打进地里来标记边界。

vocabulary.entry: post /pəʊst/ n. 柱子；桩；杆；职位 v. 张贴；发布
vocabulary.example: The fence was made of wooden posts and wire mesh.
vocabulary.translation: 这道围栏由木柱和铁丝网建成。

vocabulary.entry: fort /fɔːt/ n. 堡垒；要塞；城堡
vocabulary.example: The Roman army built a fort to defend the northern border.
vocabulary.translation: 罗马军队修建了一座堡垒来守卫北部边境。

vocabulary.entry: settlement /ˈsetlmənt/ n. 定居点；聚居地；协议
vocabulary.example: The first European settlement in this area was founded in 1607.
vocabulary.translation: 这个地区的第一个欧洲聚居地建于1607年。

vocabulary.entry: extensive /ɪkˈstensɪv/ adj. 广泛的；大量的；广阔的
vocabulary.example: The country has an extensive network of motorways and roads.
vocabulary.translation: 这个国家有遍布全国的高速公路和公路网。

vocabulary.entry: strata /ˈstrɑːtə/ n. 层；地层；阶层（stratum的复数）
vocabulary.example: The word 'street' comes from the Latin strata meaning a paved road.
vocabulary.translation: “street”一词源自古拉丁语strata，指铺砌的道路。

vocabulary.entry: paved /peɪvd/ adj. 铺砌的；铺过的 v. 铺砌（pave的过去式/过去分词）
vocabulary.example: We walked along the paved path through the park.
vocabulary.translation: 我们沿着公园内铺砌的小路散步。

vocabulary.entry: linguistics /lɪŋˈɡwɪstɪks/ n. 语言学
vocabulary.example: She studied linguistics at university and now teaches English.
vocabulary.translation: 她在大学里学的是语言学，现在教英语。

vocabulary.entry: indicate /ˈɪndɪkeɪt/ v. 表明；显示；象征；指示
vocabulary.example: Research indicates that eating fruit is good for your health.
vocabulary.translation: 研究表明吃水果对健康有益。

vocabulary.entry: origin /ˈɒrɪdʒɪn/ n. 起源；源头；出身
vocabulary.example: We need to investigate the origin of the fire.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要调查这场火灾的起因。

vocabulary.entry: castrum /ˈkæstrəm/ n. （古罗马的）军营；要塞
vocabulary.example: The Latin word castrum is the root of many English place names.
vocabulary.translation: 拉丁语单词castrum是许多英语地名的词根。

vocabulary.entry: significant /sɪɡˈnɪfɪkənt/ adj. 重要的；显著的；有意义的
vocabulary.example: There has been a significant improvement in her English skills.
vocabulary.translation: 她的英语水平有了显著的提高。

vocabulary.entry: alphabet /ˈælfəbet/ n. 字母表；字母系统
vocabulary.example: The English alphabet consists of 26 letters.
vocabulary.translation: 英语字母表由26个字母组成。

vocabulary.entry: manuscript /ˈmænjuskrɪpt/ n. 手稿；原稿；手写本
vocabulary.example: The museum has a collection of medieval manuscripts.
vocabulary.translation: 这家博物馆收藏了一批中世纪的手稿。

vocabulary.entry: version /ˈvɜːʃn/ n. 版本；形式；说法
vocabulary.example: This is an updated version of the original software.
vocabulary.translation: 这是原软件的更新版本。

vocabulary.entry: symbol /ˈsɪmbl/ n. 符号；象征；标志
vocabulary.example: The heart is a symbol of love in many cultures.
vocabulary.translation: 在许多文化中，心是爱的象征。

vocabulary.entry: pronunciation /prəˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃn/ n. 发音；读音
vocabulary.example: You need to improve your pronunciation of English words.
vocabulary.translation: 你需要改进英语单词的发音。

sentences.english: The Romans lived in Britain between 43AD and 410AD but their legacy is still felt today and not just in physical ruins.
sentences.chinese: 罗马人于公元43年至公元410年期间居住在不列颠，但他们留下的遗产至今仍能被感知到，这不仅仅体现在那些实体遗迹上。

sentences.english: The Romans left us language, including some common English words.
sentences.chinese: 罗马人还给我们留下了语言财富，其中包括一些常用的英语单词。

sentences.english: During the Roman Empire, Latin, an ancient language, was spoken in many parts of Britain.
sentences.chinese: 在罗马帝国时期，拉丁语这门古老的语言在不列颠的许多地区被使用。

sentences.english: While the Romans wrote in classical Latin, they conversed in vulgar Latin – colloquial, everyday language that was used between soldiers and in trade.
sentences.chinese: 罗马人书写时用的是古典拉丁语，但日常交谈时则使用通俗拉丁语——这种口语的日常用语在士兵之间以及贸易往来中被广泛使用。

sentences.english: Because of trade, words that stuck often relate to food and drink, such as ‘wine’, which came from the Latin ‘vinum’.
sentences.chinese: 由于贸易的缘故，留存下来的词汇往往与饮食相关，比如“wine（葡萄酒）”一词，就源自拉丁语中的“vinum”。

sentences.english: Others relate to dwellings such as ‘kitchen’, derived from the verb ‘cook’, and ‘wall’, which originally referred to a stake or post outside a fort.
sentences.chinese: 还有一些词汇与住所相关，例如“kitchen（厨房）”衍生自拉丁语中的动词“cook（烹饪）”，而“wall（墙）”最初指的是堡垒外的木桩或柱子。

sentences.english: Settlements and roads in Roman times were extensive.
sentences.chinese: 罗马时期的定居点和道路广泛分布于各地。

sentences.english: The word ‘street’, used generally as well as being used for specific names of streets, originally came from ‘strata’ which meant paved road.
sentences.chinese: “street（街道）”一词如今既可以泛指街道，也用于具体的街道名称中，它最初源自拉丁语中的“strata”，意为“铺砌的道路”。

sentences.english: On a similar note, academic research from the field of linguistics indicates many well-known place names in the UK owe their origin to Latin.
sentences.chinese: 同样，语言学领域的学术研究表明，英国许多著名的地名都起源于拉丁语。

sentences.english: For example, the Romans used ‘castrum’ to refer to a city, which developed into the common place ending -chester, -caster or -cester.
sentences.chinese: 例如，罗马人用“castrum”指代城市，这个词后来演变成了常见的地名后缀“-chester”“-caster”或“-cester”。

sentences.english: Consider Manchester. It is a former Roman fort which was known as Mamuciam.
sentences.chinese: 以曼彻斯特（Manchester）为例，它曾是一座罗马堡垒，当时名为“Mamuciam”。

sentences.english: Other places with Roman derivations include Lancaster and Leicester.
sentences.chinese: 其他罗马派生出来的地名还包括兰卡斯特（Lancaster）和莱斯特（Leicester）。

sentences.english: A significant impact on English which came from the Romans is the use of the Roman alphabet.
sentences.chinese: 罗马人对英语产生的一个重要影响是罗马字母表的使用。

sentences.english: Manuscripts of Old English texts have shown a version not unalike written English today.
sentences.chinese: 古英语文本的手稿显示，当时的书写形式与如今的书面英语已有相似之处。

sentences.english: Differences include some letters however, such as two symbols called ‘ash’ and ‘eth’.
sentences.chinese: 不过两者之间也存在一些差异，比如包含两个名为“ash（æ）”和“eth（ð）”的符号。

sentences.english: Nowadays you are more likely to see these symbols in a guide to pronunciation.
sentences.chinese: 如今，你更有可能在发音指南中看到这些符号。

sentences.english: So, even though 1,600 years have passed, the Romans live on.
sentences.chinese: 所以，即便1600多年已经过去，罗马人的印记依然延续至今。

title: Should you play fantasy sports
titleChinese: 我们应该参与梦幻运动吗？
paragraphs: Would you be good at managing a top-level sports team? Do you have the tactics and know-how to be the next Jurgen Klopp? Well, you can find out by playing fantasy sports!

While football fans across the globe observe victories, losses and draws of real matches this season, over nine million people will play Premier Fantasy Football, according to the Premier League. And it’s not just football, but also baseball, basketball and cricket to name just a few fantasy sports you can join.

In a fantasy league, you get an imaginary budget which you can spend on your squad, selecting any players that compete in the actual sport of your chosen league. Of course, better players cost more! As the real games play out, so does your fictional team.

Doesn’t sound up your street? You may well have been pressured into competing in a league against your friends or colleagues against your better judgment, but, according to research, playing fantasy sports can actually benefit you. Some people find they enjoy the camaraderie that comes with it even if they’re not a fan of the sport itself. In fact, a US Quantum Workplace survey found that co-workers who play in a fantasy league together, bond better. They scored more highly in teamwork and trust than those who play, but not with colleagues. Plus, friendly competition gives you something to chitchat over when enjoying a hard-earned rest!

Other pros are the brain training you get along with the entertainment. Strategy, tactical decision-making, budgeting and navigating large amounts of data are just some skills you need to do well in this kind of game.
So, get your team ready and good luck!

vocabulary.entry: top-level /ˌtɒp ˈlevl/ adj. 顶级的；最高水平的
vocabulary.example: She’s a top-level manager in a multinational company.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一家跨国公司的顶级管理者。

vocabulary.entry: tactic /ˈtæktɪk/ n. 策略；战术（复数：tactics）
vocabulary.example: The team used a clever tactical move to win the game.
vocabulary.translation: 这支队伍用一记巧妙的战术赢得了比赛。

vocabulary.entry: know-how /ˈnəʊ haʊ/ n. 专业技能；实际知识；诀窍
vocabulary.example: He has the technical know-how to fix the machine.
vocabulary.translation: 他有修理这台机器的专业技术知识。

vocabulary.entry: fantasy sports /ˈfæntəsi spɔːts/ 梦幻体育（虚拟体育竞技游戏）
vocabulary.example: Millions of people play fantasy sports online every year.
vocabulary.translation: 每年有数百万人在网上玩梦幻体育游戏。

vocabulary.entry: observe /əbˈzɜːv/ v. 观看；观察（比赛、事件等）
vocabulary.example: Thousands of fans came to observe the football final.
vocabulary.translation: 数千名球迷前来观看这场足球决赛。

vocabulary.entry: draw /drɔː/ n. 平局；和局（体育比赛中）
vocabulary.example: The match ended in a 1-1 draw after 90 minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 这场比赛90分钟后以1比1的平局结束。

vocabulary.entry: Premier League /ˌpremiə ˈliːɡ/ n. （英国）足球超级联赛
vocabulary.example: The Premier League is one of the most popular football leagues in the world.
vocabulary.translation: 英超联赛是世界上最受欢迎的足球联赛之一。

vocabulary.entry: cricket /ˈkrɪkɪt/ n. 板球（运动）
vocabulary.example: Cricket is a popular sport in the UK and Australia.
vocabulary.translation: 板球在英国和澳大利亚是一项受欢迎的运动。

vocabulary.entry: to name just a few /tu neɪm dʒʌst ə fjuː/ 仅举几例
vocabulary.example: There are many fruits in the shop, apples, bananas, oranges to name just a few.
vocabulary.translation: 店里有很多水果，苹果、香蕉、橙子，仅举几例。

vocabulary.entry: fantasy league /ˈfæntəsi liːɡ/ 梦幻联赛
vocabulary.example: He joined a fantasy league with his friends and won the first prize.
vocabulary.translation: 他和朋友们一起加入了一个梦幻联赛，还拿了一等奖。

vocabulary.entry: imaginary /ɪˈmædʒɪnəri/ adj. 虚构的；假想的；想象的
vocabulary.example: The child has an imaginary friend who she talks to every day.
vocabulary.translation: 这个小女孩有一个假想的朋友，她每天都会和这个朋友说话。

vocabulary.entry: budget /ˈbʌdʒɪt/ n. 预算
vocabulary.example: We have a tight budget for the school trip this year.
vocabulary.translation: 今年我们学校旅行的预算很紧张。

vocabulary.entry: squad /skwɒd/ n. （体育）队伍；阵容
vocabulary.example: The coach selected a strong squad for the upcoming tournament.
vocabulary.translation: 教练为即将到来的锦标赛挑选了一支强劲的队伍。

vocabulary.entry: compete /kəmˈpiːt/ v. 竞争；参赛
vocabulary.example: Over 200 athletes will compete in the swimming competition.
vocabulary.translation: 有200多名运动员将参加这场游泳比赛。

vocabulary.entry: play out /pleɪ aʊt/ （事件、比赛）上演；发生；展开
vocabulary.example: We watched as the drama played out on the football pitch.
vocabulary.translation: 我们看着球场上的这场精彩对决徐徐展开。

vocabulary.entry: fictional /ˈfɪkʃənl/ adj. 虚构的；假想的

vocabulary.entry: pressure /ˈpreʃə(r)/ v. 逼迫；迫使

vocabulary.translation: 她被同事们逼着同意了这个计划。

vocabulary.entry: colleague /ˈkɒliːɡ/ n. 同事；同僚

vocabulary.translation: 我和办公室的几个同事一起去吃了午饭。

vocabulary.term: against one's better judgment 明知不妥却仍做；违背自己的判断
vocabulary.entry: against one's better judgment 明知不妥却仍做；违背自己的判断
vocabulary.example: Against my better judgment, I lent him the money and never got it back.
vocabulary.translation: 我明知不妥还是借了钱给他，结果再也没要回来。

vocabulary.entry: benefit /ˈbenɪfɪt/ v. 使受益；得益
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise benefits both the body and the mind.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动对身心都有益。

vocabulary.translation: 这个团队的成员之间相处得十分融洽，充满了团队友爱。

vocabulary.translation: 良好的团队合作是这个项目成功的关键。

vocabulary.translation: 这场比赛只是朋友间的一点友好竞争而已。

vocabulary.entry: chitchat /ˈtʃɪttʃæt/ v. 闲聊；闲谈

vocabulary.translation: 居家办公的最大好处是它带来的灵活性。

sentences.chinese: 而且梦幻体育的种类不止足球，棒球、篮球、板球等也都在可选之列。

sentences.chinese: 在梦幻体育联赛中，你会获得一笔虚拟预算，用来组建自己的球队阵容，你可以从所选联赛的真实参赛球员中任意挑选。

sentences.chinese: 当然，实力更强的球员身价也更高！

sentences.english: As the real games play out, so does your fictional team.
sentences.chinese: 随着现实中的比赛推进，你这支虚拟球队的战绩也会同步更新。

sentences.chinese: 这听起来适合你吗？

sentences.english: You may well have been pressured into competing in a league against your friends or colleagues against your better judgment, but, according to research, playing fantasy sports can actually benefit you.
sentences.chinese: 你或许曾拗不过他人，不得已和朋友或同事组队参赛，但研究表明，玩梦幻体育游戏其实对你大有裨益。

sentences.english: Some people find they enjoy the camaraderie that comes with it even if they’re not a fan of the sport itself.
sentences.chinese: 有些人发现，即便自己并非这项运动的爱好者，也能享受游戏带来的团队情谊。

sentences.english: In fact, a US Quantum Workplace survey found that co-workers who play in a fantasy league together, bond better.
sentences.chinese: 美国昆腾（量子）职场咨询公司的一项调查显示，一同参与梦幻体育联赛的同事，彼此之间的关系会更加融洽。

sentences.english: They scored more highly in teamwork and trust than those who play, but not with colleagues.
sentences.chinese: 在团队协作和信任度的评分上，他们比那些和非同事组队的玩家要高得多。

sentences.english: Plus, friendly competition gives you something to chitchat over when enjoying a hard-earned rest!
sentences.chinese: 此外，这种友好的竞争还能为你在来之不易的休息时间里，增添不少闲聊的话题！

sentences.english: Other pros are the brain training you get along with the entertainment.
sentences.chinese: 除了娱乐之外，这类游戏还能锻炼你的脑力。

sentences.english: Strategy, tactical decision-making, budgeting and navigating large amounts of data are just some skills you need to do well in this kind of game.
sentences.chinese: 要想在游戏中表现出色，你需要掌握策略制定、战术决策、预算规划以及海量数据分析等多项技能。

sentences.english: So, get your team ready and good luck!
sentences.chinese: 所以，赶紧组建你的球队，祝你好运！

title: Smartphone addiction
paragraphs: How would you survive without your smartphone? For many of us, it’s the gadget we’re most hooked on – looking at it hundreds of times a day. We depend on it to perform a multitude of tasks and to connect with our friends and family. But have we become addicted to our phones?

Certainly, the inventor of the first mobile phone, American engineer Martin Cooper, thinks we might be. In a BBC interview, he suggested people should stop scrolling and “get a life”. But of course, once we start doom scrolling or watching videos, we just can’t kick the habit. Psychologist and author Jean Twenge says we’re all guilty of “compulsively checking [our] phone if [we’re] waiting for a text or getting really into social media then kind of, looking up and realising that an hour has passed.” There’s even a word – a phubber – to describe a person who ignores the real people around them because they are concentrating on their phones.

But does it matter if we make the most of this technology? Possibly, because like a drug, the problem arises when it is withdrawn. A study from King’s College London found young people they studied couldn’t control the amount of time they spend on their phone. Such addictive behaviour means that people become ‘panicky’ or ‘upset’ if they are denied constant access, which can cause anxiety and mental health issues.

Interestingly, another study by the London School of Economics and Political Science suggests we don’t just look at our phones because we are prompted to by a text or email. The people they studied felt automatically urged to interact with their phone, just as a smoker would light a cigarette. Prof Saadi Lahlou, co-author of the study, told the BBC: “We must learn tricks to avoid the temptation when we want to concentrate or have good social relations.”

One solution could be an app that rewards students for time spent away from their phones. Another option is converting your smartphone to a dumbphone that has none of the intoxicating distractions on it. But mainly, perhaps, we just need to look up more and reconnect with the real world!

sentences.english: How would you survive without your smartphone?
sentences.chinese: 如果没有智能手机，你该如何生活？

sentences.english: For many of us, it’s the gadget we’re most hooked on – looking at it hundreds of times a day.
sentences.chinese: 对我们很多人来说，智能手机是最让我们着迷的设备——每天要看上数百次。

sentences.english: We depend on it to perform a multitude of tasks and to connect with our friends and family.
sentences.chinese: 我们依靠它完成各种各样的任务，以及与亲友保持联系。

sentences.english: But have we become addicted to our phones?
sentences.chinese: 但我们是否已经对手机上瘾了呢？

sentences.english: Certainly, the inventor of the first mobile phone, American engineer Martin Cooper, thinks we might be.
sentences.chinese: 第一部移动电话的发明者、美国工程师马丁·库珀认为我们可能已经上瘾了。

sentences.english: In a BBC interview, he suggested people should stop scrolling and “get a life”.
sentences.chinese: 他在接受BBC采访时建议人们应该停止刷屏，“做点有意义的事情”。

sentences.english: But of course, once we start doom scrolling or watching videos, we just can’t kick the habit.
sentences.chinese: 但当然，一旦我们开始“末日刷屏”或是看视频，就很难戒掉这个习惯。

sentences.english: Psychologist and author Jean Twenge says we’re all guilty of “compulsively checking [our] phone if [we’re] waiting for a text or getting really into social media then kind of, looking up and realising that an hour has passed.”
sentences.chinese: 心理学家兼作家简·特温吉表示，我们都有这样的毛病：“等短信的时候会忍不住频繁查看手机，或者沉迷社交媒体，抬头时才发现一个小时已经过去了。”

sentences.english: There’s even a word – a phubber – to describe a person who ignores the real people around them because they are concentrating on their phones.
sentences.chinese: 甚至还有一个专门的词——“低头族”，用来形容那些因为专注于手机而忽视身边人的人。

sentences.english: But does it matter if we make the most of this technology?
sentences.chinese: 但我们充分利用这项技术，真的有问题吗？

sentences.english: Possibly, because like a drug, the problem arises when it is withdrawn.
sentences.chinese: 或许是有的，因为就像毒品一样，当手机被拿走时，问题就出现了。

sentences.english: A study from King’s College London found young people they studied couldn’t control the amount of time they spend on their phone.
sentences.chinese: 伦敦国王学院的一项研究发现，参与调查的年轻人无法控制自己使用手机的时长。

sentences.english: Such addictive behaviour means that people become ‘panicky’ or ‘upset’ if they are denied constant access, which can cause anxiety and mental health issues.
sentences.chinese: 这种成瘾行为意味着，当人们无法随时使用手机时，会变得“恐慌”或“烦躁”，进而可能引发焦虑和心理健康问题。

sentences.english: Interestingly, another study by the London School of Economics and Political Science suggests we don’t just look at our phones because we are prompted to by a text or email.
sentences.chinese: 有趣的是，另一项由伦敦政治经济学院进行的研究表明，我们看手机不只是因为收到了短信或邮件的提醒。

sentences.english: The people they studied felt automatically urged to interact with their phone, just as a smoker would light a cigarette.
sentences.chinese: 参与研究的人表示，自己会下意识地想要去碰手机，就像吸烟者会习惯性地点烟一样。

sentences.english: Prof Saadi Lahlou, co-author of the study, told the BBC: “We must learn tricks to avoid the temptation when we want to concentrate or have good social relations.”
sentences.chinese: 该研究的合著者萨阿迪·拉卢教授告诉BBC：“当我们想要集中注意力或是维持良好的社交关系时，必须学会一些技巧来抵御这种诱惑。”

sentences.english: One solution could be an app that rewards students for time spent away from their phones.
sentences.chinese: 一种解决办法是开发一款应用，奖励那些放下手机的学生。

sentences.english: Another option is converting your smartphone to a dumbphone that has none of the intoxicating distractions on it.
sentences.chinese: 另一种选择是把智能手机改成功能机，这类手机没有那些让人沉迷的干扰项。

sentences.english: But mainly, perhaps, we just need to look up more and reconnect with the real world!
sentences.chinese: 但或许，最主要的办法还是我们需要多抬头看看，重新与现实世界建立联系！

title: Can you delay ageing with a positive attitude
titleChinese: 积极的态度可以延缓衰老吗？
paragraphs: When do you think ‘middle age’ starts? What about ‘old age’? Unsurprisingly, the answer to these questions will depend on your culture, as well as how old you are when someone asks you. What is perhaps more surprising is that the answer to these questions could have an impact on how quickly your body begins to age.

In 2003, the researchers Hannah Kuper and Sir Michael Marmot carried out a wide-ranging study in which participants were asked the question: when does old age start? They then followed up with the participants six to nine years later and found that those who had thought old age began earlier were more likely to be in poor physical health.

But how could someone’s answer to a question about age possibly have an impact on their health? It might be that the question prompts people to think about their physical health, underlying health issues or poor lifestyle, which might then make them feel that old age is coming sooner. People who say that old age sets in earlier, may also be more fatalistic and less likely to visit a doctor or to adopt healthier routines. It’s even possible that the stress of having negative thoughts about ageing, contributes to more health problems.

So, this is what happens when we think negatively about ageing, but what happens when we think positively? People who think old age starts later, may be more conscious about their health and fitness and therefore take steps to stay in better shape. They may see their twilight years as an opportunity to learn new things and make new plans. If they believe they are younger, they therefore behave in younger ways, creating a virtuous circle. Whatever the reason, according to data from the Ohio Longitudinal Study of Ageing and Retirement, people who think positively about ageing live longer on average.

Of course, none of this research means that a positive attitude can magically stop the ageing process – our bodies get older with each passing year, after all. But it seems that if we try to be healthier and if we believe that there are still things we can do in old age, we might live longer and enjoy ourselves more too.

vocabulary.translation: 这项检查旨在找出他慢性疼痛的潜在原因。

vocabulary.translation: 他对生活抱着听天由命的态度，从不愿尝试改变自己的处境。

vocabulary.entry: adopt /əˈdɒpt/ v. 采取；采纳；养成（习惯）

vocabulary.translation: 她决定对工作采取一种更积极的态度。

vocabulary.entry: routine /ruːˈtiːn/ n. 常规；惯例；日常安排 adj. 常规的

vocabulary.translation: 我需要建立规律的晨间作息，让自己更有效率。

vocabulary.entry: negative thought /ˈneɡətɪv θɔːt/ n. 消极想法；负面想法

vocabulary.translation: 放下消极想法，关注积极的一面，这一点很重要。

vocabulary.entry: ageing /ˈeɪdʒɪŋ/ n. 衰老；变老 adj. 衰老的；老龄化的

vocabulary.entry: positively /ˈpɒzətɪvli/ adv. 积极地；肯定地；乐观地

vocabulary.entry: take steps /teɪk steps/ 采取措施；采取行动

vocabulary.entry: virtuous circle /ˈvɜːtʃuəs ˈsɜːkl/ n. 良性循环
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise leads to better health, which in turn encourages more exercise—a virtuous circle.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动带来更好的健康状况，这又会促使人们更多地运动，形成一个良性循环。

vocabulary.entry: longitudinal /ˌlɒŋɡɪˈtjuːdɪnl/ adj. 纵向的；长期追踪的（学术研究）
vocabulary.example: The team conducted a longitudinal study of children’s development over 10 years.
vocabulary.translation: 该团队对儿童的发展进行了一项为期10年的纵向研究。

vocabulary.entry: retirement /rɪˈtaɪəmənt/ n. 退休；退役
vocabulary.example: He saved a lot of money for his retirement.
vocabulary.translation: 他为退休存了一大笔钱。

vocabulary.entry: on average /ɒn ˈævərɪdʒ/ 平均而言；平均来说
vocabulary.example: On average, people spend two hours a day on social media.
vocabulary.translation: 平均而言，人们每天花两小时在社交媒体上。

vocabulary.entry: attitude /ˈætɪtjuːd/ n. 态度；看法；心态
vocabulary.example: Her positive attitude helped her get through the difficult time.
vocabulary.translation: 她积极的心态帮她度过了那段艰难的时光。

vocabulary.entry: magically /ˈmædʒɪkli/ adv. 神奇地；魔法般地；不可思议地
vocabulary.example: The pain disappeared magically after she took the medicine.
vocabulary.translation: 她吃完药后，疼痛竟神奇地消失了。

vocabulary.entry: ageing process /ˈeɪdʒɪŋ ˈprəʊses/ n. 衰老过程
vocabulary.example: Eating more fruits and vegetables can slow down the human ageing process.
vocabulary.translation: 多吃水果蔬菜可以延缓人类的衰老过程。

vocabulary.entry: each passing year /iːtʃ ˈpɑːsɪŋ jɪə(r)/ 一年又一年；每过一年
vocabulary.example: Each passing year, we realize more the importance of family.
vocabulary.translation: 一年又一年，我们越发体会到家庭的重要性。

vocabulary.entry: enjoy oneself /ɪnˈdʒɔɪ wʌnˈself/ 过得愉快；享受生活；玩得开心
vocabulary.example: We really enjoyed ourselves at the weekend party.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在周末的派对上玩得非常开心。

sentences.english: When do you think ‘middle age’ starts?
sentences.chinese: 你认为“中年”始于何时？

sentences.english: What about ‘old age’?
sentences.chinese: “老年”呢？

sentences.english: Unsurprisingly, the answer to these questions will depend on your culture, as well as how old you are when someone asks you.
sentences.chinese: 不出所料，这些问题的答案会因文化背景而异，同时也取决于被问到这个问题时你的年龄。

sentences.english: What is perhaps more surprising is that the answer to these questions could have an impact on how quickly your body begins to age.
sentences.chinese: 但或许更令人惊讶的是，对这些问题的回答，竟然会影响你身体衰老的速度。

sentences.english: In 2003, the researchers Hannah Kuper and Sir Michael Marmot carried out a wide-ranging study in which participants were asked the question: when does old age start?
sentences.chinese: 2003年，研究人员汉娜·库珀和迈克尔·马尔莫爵士开展了一项大范围研究。研究中，他们向参与者提出了一个问题：老年从什么时候开始？

sentences.english: They then followed up with the participants six to nine years later and found that those who had thought old age began earlier were more likely to be in poor physical health.
sentences.chinese: 六到九年后，研究人员对这些参与者进行了追踪调查，结果发现，那些认为老年到来时间更早的人，身体健康状况不佳的可能性更高。

sentences.english: But how could someone’s answer to a question about age possibly have an impact on their health?
sentences.chinese: 但一个人对年龄相关问题的回答，怎么会影响到自身健康呢？

sentences.english: It might be that the question prompts people to think about their physical health, underlying health issues or poor lifestyle, which might then make them feel that old age is coming sooner.
sentences.chinese: 可能是这个问题促使人们开始审视自己的身体健康状况、潜在的健康隐患或是不良的生活习惯，进而让他们觉得老年正在加速到来。

sentences.english: People who say that old age sets in earlier, may also be more fatalistic and less likely to visit a doctor or to adopt healthier routines.
sentences.chinese: 那些认为老年来得更早的人，或许也更具宿命论思想，他们不太愿意去看医生，也不太会养成更健康的生活习惯。

sentences.english: It’s even possible that the stress of having negative thoughts about ageing, contributes to more health problems.
sentences.chinese: 甚至有可能，对衰老抱有负面想法所产生的压力，会引发更多的健康问题。

sentences.english: So, this is what happens when we think negatively about ageing, but what happens when we think positively?
sentences.chinese: 以上是我们对衰老持消极态度时会出现的情况，那如果我们抱有积极心态，又会怎样呢？

sentences.english: People who think old age starts later, may be more conscious about their health and fitness and therefore take steps to stay in better shape.
sentences.chinese: 那些认为老年开始得更晚的人，可能会更关注自身的健康和体能状况，从而采取措施保持良好的身体状态。

sentences.english: They may see their twilight years as an opportunity to learn new things and make new plans.
sentences.chinese: 他们会把晚年时光看作是学习新事物、制定新计划的机会。

sentences.english: If they believe they are younger, they therefore behave in younger ways, creating a virtuous circle.
sentences.chinese: 如果他们相信自己还很年轻，就会以更年轻化的方式行事，进而形成一个良性循环。

sentences.english: Whatever the reason, according to data from the Ohio Longitudinal Study of Ageing and Retirement, people who think positively about ageing live longer on average.
sentences.chinese: 无论原因是什么，俄亥俄州老龄化与退休纵向研究的数据显示，对衰老持积极态度的人，平均寿命会更长。

sentences.english: Of course, none of this research means that a positive attitude can magically stop the ageing process – our bodies get older with each passing year, after all.
sentences.chinese: 当然，这些研究并不意味着积极的心态能神奇地阻止衰老进程——毕竟，我们的身体每年都在变老。

sentences.english: But it seems that if we try to be healthier and if we believe that there are still things we can do in old age, we might live longer and enjoy ourselves more too.
sentences.chinese: 但似乎可以确定的是，如果我们努力保持健康，并且相信自己在晚年仍然有很多事情可以做，我们就有可能活得更长久，也能更享受生活。

title: Creatures of the deep
paragraphs: The ocean covers over 70% of the surface of our planet, though, according to the National Ocean Service, 95% of it remains unexplored. This is because under the surface is a dark and hostile environment with unrelenting high pressure, freezing temperatures and bizarre creatures in the depths.

The Census of Marine Life reports more than 17,000 species living in the deep sea. The Greenland shark can live in depths of 7,200 feet and is a rarely seen Arctic predator said to live to 400 years old and reach 23 feet in length. In order to battle the icy depths, Greenland sharks have chemicals in their skin which prevent ice crystals from forming on their body.

Another deep-sea creature is the giant squid, an animal that remains a mystery to scientists despite being the largest invertebrate on Earth. Living far below the surface, what we know has largely come from carcasses being washed ashore. Marine biologists have found that they feed on fish, squid and possibly even small whales. They find prey using eyes which are ten inches wide, roughly the size of a dinner plate!

Other unusual creatures include the vampire squid, which lives 2000 to 3000 feet under the ocean and is so-called because of its dark cloak that connects its eight arms. There is also the dumbo octopus, named due to its resemblance to the elephant from the 1943 Disney film Dumbo, with its protruding ears. Another unique creature is the anglerfish known for the light that hangs from its head.
So, enjoy swimming, but don’t venture too far down – you never know what is lurking beneath!

vocabulary.entry: unexplored /ˌʌnɪkˈsplɔːd/ adj. 未被探索的；未开发的
vocabulary.example: Large areas of the rainforest remain unexplored.
vocabulary.translation: 热带雨林的大片区域仍未被探索。

vocabulary.entry: hostile /ˈhɒstaɪl/ adj. （环境）恶劣的；充满敌意的；敌对的
vocabulary.example: The team faced a hostile environment in the desert.
vocabulary.translation: 这支队伍在沙漠中遭遇了恶劣的环境。

vocabulary.entry: unrelenting /ʌnrɪˈlentɪŋ/ adj. 持续不断的；不松懈的；无情的
vocabulary.example: We struggled against the unrelenting wind all day.
vocabulary.translation: 我们一整天都在和持续不断的大风抗争。

vocabulary.entry: freezing /ˈfriːzɪŋ/ adj. 极冷的；冰冻的
vocabulary.example: The temperature dropped to freezing last night.
vocabulary.translation: 昨晚气温降到了冰点。

vocabulary.entry: bizarre /bɪˈzɑː(r)/ adj. 奇异的；古怪的；怪诞的
vocabulary.example: She told a bizarre story about her trip to the mountains.
vocabulary.translation: 她讲了一个关于她登山之旅的离奇故事。

vocabulary.entry: depth /depθ/ n. 深处；深海；深渊
vocabulary.example: The diver descended to a depth of 50 metres.
vocabulary.translation: 潜水员下潜到了50米的深海处。

vocabulary.entry: Census of Marine Life /ˈsensəs ɒv məˈriːn laɪf/ n. 海洋生物普查
vocabulary.example: The Census of Marine Life has discovered thousands of new sea species.
vocabulary.translation: 海洋生物普查已经发现了数千种新的海洋物种。

vocabulary.entry: species /ˈspiːʃiːz/ n. 物种；种类
vocabulary.example: This rare species of bird is found only in the Amazon.
vocabulary.translation: 这种珍稀鸟类只在亚马逊地区被发现。

vocabulary.entry: Greenland shark /ˈɡriːnlænd ʃɑːk/ n. 格陵兰睡鲨
vocabulary.example: The Greenland shark is one of the longest-living vertebrates on Earth.
vocabulary.translation: 格陵兰睡鲨是地球上寿命最长的脊椎动物之一。

vocabulary.entry: Arctic /ˈɑːktɪk/ adj. 北极的；北冰洋的 n. 北极地区
vocabulary.example: Polar bears live in the Arctic region.
vocabulary.translation: 北极熊生活在北极地区。

vocabulary.entry: predator /ˈpredətə(r)/ n. 捕食者；食肉动物
vocabulary.example: Lions are top predators in the African savanna.
vocabulary.translation: 狮子是非洲稀树草原上的顶级捕食者。

vocabulary.entry: length /leŋθ/ n. 身长；长度；持续时间
vocabulary.example: The snake can reach a length of two metres.
vocabulary.translation: 这种蛇的身长可达两米。

vocabulary.entry: battle /ˈbætl/ v. 对抗；搏斗；作战 n. 战斗；战役
vocabulary.example: The plant battles against the harsh sun to survive.
vocabulary.translation: 这种植物为了生存对抗着强烈的阳光。

vocabulary.entry: icy /ˈaɪsi/ adj. 冰冷的；结满冰的

vocabulary.translation: 我们不得不小心翼翼地走在结冰的路上。

vocabulary.entry: chemical /ˈkemɪkl/ n. 化学物质 adj. 化学的
vocabulary.example: The plant produces a special chemical to protect itself from insects.
vocabulary.translation: 这种植物会产生一种特殊的化学物质来保护自己免受昆虫侵害。

vocabulary.entry: crystal /ˈkrɪstl/ n. 晶体；水晶

vocabulary.translation: 水分蒸发后会形成盐晶体。

vocabulary.entry: giant squid /ˈdʒaɪənt skwɪd/ n. 大王乌贼

vocabulary.translation: 大王乌贼是最神秘的海洋生物之一。

vocabulary.entry: mystery /ˈmɪstəri/ n. 谜；神秘的事物；奥秘

vocabulary.translation: 这座古老遗迹的起源仍是一个谜。

vocabulary.entry: invertebrate /ɪnˈvɜːtɪbrət/ n. 无脊椎动物 adj. 无脊椎的

vocabulary.translation: 一头鲸鱼的尸体被冲上岸后，这片海滩就关闭了。

vocabulary.translation: 这位海洋生物学家花了数年时间研究珊瑚礁。

vocabulary.entry: dinner plate /ˈdɪnə pleɪt/ n. 餐盘；正餐盘

vocabulary.entry: resemblance /rɪˈzembləns/ n. 相似；相像

sentences.english: Another unique creature is the anglerfish known for the light that hangs from its head.
sentences.chinese: 另外一种独特的生物是琵琶鱼，它因头部悬挂着一个发光器官而闻名。

sentences.english: So, enjoy swimming, but don’t venture too far down – you never know what is lurking beneath!
