title: Why do we laugh
paragraphs: What things make you laugh? There are many things that make us chuckle or burst into laughter. This natural show of emotion gives off signals that we are happy, we find something humorous or even that we’re just a barrel of laughs! Gelotologists have been looking at why we do it and what the benefits are.

Laughter is a very primitive way of making a sound. When we do it, we make very strange noises – from wheezes and squeaks to gasps and snorts – and each sound simply reflects the muscles in the chest squeezing out air from our ribcages under very high pressure.

Most of the time our laughter is involuntary and contagious, particularly between friends. Neuroscientist, Sophie Scott, told the BBC that it’s “a social emotion. It’s better to laugh with people we like.” She defines two types of laughter – spontaneous laughter, where we laugh instantly and uncontrollably, and conversational laughter – where we laugh together with friends. Research found, on average, people laugh seven times for every ten minutes of conversation.

The BBC World Service programme Crowd Science examined the science of laughter. It wanted to know what caused this highly infectious repetitive action. It found we use laughter to show others that we’re being playful and non-threatening, and this serves to make and maintain social bonds. Also, people outside of our social group can understand the relationship between the laughers by the sound of our chuckles.

While our health is no laughing matter, research has found a good guffaw can help our body and mind – it can make us feel good and relax our bodies. It also helps us manage pain and improve our immune system. That’s why laughter therapy is being used as an alternative to conventional treatments. But generally, our ability to laugh is out of our control. When you start doing it, just go with the flow and others will join in.

vocabulary.entry: chuckle /ˈtʃʌkl/ v. 轻声笑；咯咯地笑
vocabulary.example: He chuckled at the funny story in the book.
vocabulary.translation: 他对着书里的有趣故事轻声笑了起来。

vocabulary.entry: burst into laughter /bɜːst ɪntu ˈlɑːftə(r)/ 突然大笑；放声大笑
vocabulary.example: The children burst into laughter when they saw the silly clown.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子们看到那个滑稽的小丑，突然放声大笑。

vocabulary.entry: a barrel of laughs /ə ˈbærəl ɒv lɑːfts/ （口语）非常有趣的人或事；笑料百出的事物
vocabulary.example: My new colleague is a real barrel of laughs, we have fun working together.
vocabulary.translation: 我的新同事特别有趣，我们一起工作很开心。

vocabulary.entry: gelotologist /dʒəˌləʊtəˈlɒdʒɪst/ n. 笑学家；研究笑的心理学学者
vocabulary.example: The gelotologist has spent years studying the effects of laughter on human health.
vocabulary.translation: 这位笑学家花了数年时间研究笑对人类健康的影响。

vocabulary.entry: primitive /ˈprɪmətɪv/ adj. 原始的；本能的；与生俱来的
vocabulary.example: Crying is a primitive reaction to pain in human beings.
vocabulary.translation: 哭泣是人类对疼痛的一种本能反应。

vocabulary.entry: wheeze /hwiːz/ n. 气喘般的笑声；呼哧声
vocabulary.example: A loud wheeze escaped her as she laughed at the joke.
vocabulary.translation: 她听到笑话笑起来，发出了一声响亮的气喘似的笑声。

vocabulary.entry: squeak /skwiːk/ n. 尖细的笑声；吱吱声
vocabulary.example: There was a little squeak of laughter from the back of the classroom.
vocabulary.translation: 教室后排传来一声尖细的笑声。

vocabulary.entry: gasp /ɡɑːsp/ n. 喘着气的笑声；倒吸一口气的声音
vocabulary.example: Her laugh was a series of gasps as she tried to catch her breath.
vocabulary.translation: 她笑得喘不过气，一连串的喘笑从嘴里发出来。

vocabulary.entry: snort /snɔːt/ n. 哼笑；鼻息式的笑声
vocabulary.example: He let out a snort of laughter when he heard the ridiculous excuse.
vocabulary.translation: 听到那个荒唐的借口，他发出了一声哼笑。

vocabulary.entry: ribcage /ˈrɪbkeɪdʒ/ n. 胸腔；胸廓
vocabulary.example: The heavy cough made his ribcage ache terribly.
vocabulary.translation: 剧烈的咳嗽让他的胸腔疼得厉害。

vocabulary.entry: involuntary /ɪnˈvɒləntri/ adj. 无意识的；不自觉的；非自愿的
vocabulary.example: She gave an involuntary jump when the door slammed shut.
vocabulary.translation: 门砰地关上时，她不自觉地跳了一下。

vocabulary.entry: contagious /kənˈteɪdʒəs/ adj. （情绪、行为）有感染力的；易传播的
vocabulary.example: Her cheerful smile is so contagious that everyone around her feels happy.
vocabulary.translation: 她灿烂的笑容很有感染力，身边的人都觉得心情愉悦。

vocabulary.entry: neuroscientist /ˌnjʊərəʊˈsaɪəntɪst/ n. 神经科学家
vocabulary.example: The neuroscientist is researching how the brain responds to different emotions.
vocabulary.translation: 这位神经科学家正在研究大脑对不同情绪的反应。

vocabulary.entry: spontaneous /spɒnˈteɪniəs/ adj. 自发的；不由自主的；自然产生的
vocabulary.example: The crowd broke into spontaneous applause when the singer finished the song.
vocabulary.translation: 歌手唱完歌后，人群自发地鼓起掌来。

vocabulary.entry: instantly /ˈɪnstəntli/ adv. 立刻；马上；瞬间地
vocabulary.example: He instantly recognized his old friend from the photo.
vocabulary.translation: 他从照片里一眼就认出了老朋友。

vocabulary.entry: uncontrollably /ˌʌnkənˈtrəʊləbli/ adv. 无法控制地；不由自主地
vocabulary.example: She started crying uncontrollably when she heard the bad news.
vocabulary.translation: 听到这个坏消息，她忍不住失声痛哭。

vocabulary.entry: conversational /ˌkɒnvəˈseɪʃənl/ adj. 交谈的；会话的；闲谈式的
vocabulary.example: The book uses simple conversational English that is easy to understand.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书使用简单的闲谈式英语，通俗易懂。

vocabulary.entry: infectious /ɪnˈfekʃəs/ adj. （情绪）富有感染力的；传染性的
vocabulary.example: Her infectious laughter made everyone in the room smile.
vocabulary.translation: 她那富有感染力的笑声让房间里的所有人都笑了。

vocabulary.entry: repetitive /rɪˈpetətɪv/ adj. 重复的；反复的
vocabulary.example: The job involves a lot of repetitive tasks like data entry.
vocabulary.translation: 这份工作包含很多像数据录入这样的重复性工作。

vocabulary.entry: non-threatening /ˌnɒn ˈθretnɪŋ/ adj. 无威胁的；平和的；友善的
vocabulary.example: The dog has a non-threatening appearance and is very friendly to kids.
vocabulary.translation: 这只狗看起来毫无攻击性，对孩子也十分友善。

vocabulary.entry: social bond /ˈsəʊʃl bɒnd/ n. 社会纽带；人际关系；情感联结
vocabulary.example: Shared experiences help to strengthen the social bond between family members.
vocabulary.translation: 共同的经历有助于加深家庭成员之间的情感联结。

vocabulary.entry: no laughing matter /nəʊ ˈlɑːfɪŋ ˈmætə(r)/ 不是开玩笑的事；严肃的事
vocabulary.example: Climate change is no laughing matter and we all need to take action.
vocabulary.translation: 气候变化不是小事，我们所有人都需要采取行动。

vocabulary.entry: guffaw /ɡʌˈfɔː/ n. 大笑；哄笑；爽朗的笑
vocabulary.example: He let out a loud guffaw when he saw the funny picture.
vocabulary.translation: 看到那张有趣的图片，他发出了一阵爽朗的大笑。

vocabulary.entry: immune system /ɪˈmjuːn ˈsɪstəm/ n. 免疫系统
vocabulary.example: Eating a balanced diet is important for building a strong immune system.
vocabulary.translation: 均衡饮食对打造强健的免疫系统至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: laughter therapy /ˈlɑːftə(r) ˈθerəpi/ n. 笑声疗法；笑疗
vocabulary.example: Laughter therapy is used in some hospitals to help patients reduce stress.
vocabulary.translation: 一些医院会采用笑声疗法帮助患者缓解压力。

sentences.english: What things make you laugh?
sentences.chinese: 什么事物会让你发笑？

sentences.english: There are many things that make us chuckle or burst into laughter.
sentences.chinese: 生活中有很多事情能让我们忍不住轻笑或是捧腹大笑。

sentences.english: This natural show of emotion gives off signals that we are happy, we find something humorous or even that we’re just a barrel of laughs!
sentences.chinese: 这种自然的情绪表达会传递出我们很开心、觉得某件事很有趣，甚至我们是开心果的信号！

sentences.english: Gelotologists have been looking at why we do it and what the benefits are.
sentences.chinese: 笑学家们一直在研究人类发笑的原因以及笑能带来的益处。

sentences.english: Laughter is a very primitive way of making a sound.
sentences.chinese: 笑是一种非常原始的发声方式。

sentences.english: When we do it, we make very strange noises – from wheezes and squeaks to gasps and snorts – and each sound simply reflects the muscles in the chest squeezing out air from our ribcages under very high pressure.
sentences.chinese: 当我们笑的时候，会发出各种奇怪的声音——从喘息声、尖细的笑声到倒吸气声、鼻息声都有，每一种声音都源于胸腔肌肉在高压下将空气挤出胸腔的过程。

sentences.english: Most of the time our laughter is involuntary and contagious, particularly between friends.
sentences.chinese: 大多数时候，我们的笑是无意识且具有感染力的，在朋友之间尤其如此。

sentences.english: Neuroscientist, Sophie Scott, told the BBC that it’s “a social emotion.
sentences.chinese: 神经科学家索菲·斯科特在接受BBC采访时表示，笑“是一种社交性的情绪。

sentences.english: It’s better to laugh with people we like.”
sentences.chinese: 和自己喜欢的人一起笑，会更愉悦”。

sentences.english: She defines two types of laughter – spontaneous laughter, where we laugh instantly and uncontrollably, and conversational laughter – where we laugh together with friends.
sentences.chinese: 她将笑分为两种类型——自发性的笑，也就是那种不由自主、瞬间爆发的笑，以及交谈式的笑，即和朋友们一起时产生的笑声。

sentences.english: Research found, on average, people laugh seven times for every ten minutes of conversation.
sentences.chinese: 研究发现，人们平均每十分钟的对话中就会笑七次。

sentences.english: The BBC World Service programme Crowd Science examined the science of laughter.
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司全球服务节目《大众科学》探究了笑的科学原理。

sentences.english: It wanted to know what caused this highly infectious repetitive action.
sentences.chinese: 该节目试图找出这种极具感染力的重复性行为背后的原因。

sentences.english: It found we use laughter to show others that we’re being playful and non-threatening, and this serves to make and maintain social bonds.
sentences.chinese: 研究发现，我们通过笑向他人传递出“我们在开玩笑，没有恶意”的信号，这有助于建立和维系社交关系。

sentences.english: Also, people outside of our social group can understand the relationship between the laughers by the sound of our chuckles.
sentences.chinese: 此外，社交圈子之外的人也能通过笑声的特点，判断出发笑者之间的关系。

sentences.english: While our health is no laughing matter, research has found a good guffaw can help our body and mind – it can make us feel good and relax our bodies. It also helps us manage pain and improve our immune system.
sentences.chinese: 虽然健康问题绝非儿戏，但研究发现，开怀大笑对我们的身心都大有裨益——它能让我们心情愉悦，放松身体，还有助于缓解疼痛、增强免疫系统。

sentences.english: That’s why laughter therapy is being used as an alternative to conventional treatments.
sentences.chinese: 这也是为什么笑声疗法正被用作传统疗法的替代方案。

sentences.english: But generally, our ability to laugh is out of our control.
sentences.chinese: 不过通常来说，我们发笑的本能是不受控制的。

sentences.english: When you start doing it, just go with the flow and others will join in.
sentences.chinese: 当你笑起来的时候，只管顺其自然，身边的人自然会跟着一起笑。

title: Can chocolate ever be healthy
titleChinese: 巧克力能成为健康食品吗？
paragraphs: When you think of foods that are good for you, chocolate may not be high up on your list. But, there has been a lot of research into dark chocolate, which shows that it does, in fact, have health benefits.

Chocolate is made by roasting cacao seeds, which come from the cacao tree. After being processed into cocoa solids, cocoa butter and combined with sugar and sometimes dairy, chocolate is the result. To know how dark the chocolate is, and to determine the potential health benefits, we need to look at the level of cocoa solids it contains.

If dark chocolate has a high cocoa content, labelled as a percentage, it may be dense in minerals such as magnesium and iron. According to a 2011 study comparing cacao seeds to ‘super fruits’ such as cranberries and pomegranates, dark chocolate may have high levels of antioxidants. Other research includes a 2018 study which found that dark chocolate could significantly reduce inflammation in people with type 2 diabetes.

But companies trying to market dark chocolate as a healthy snack may have a difficult time – the higher the cocoa content, the more bitter the taste. Plus, commercial dark chocolate tends to be high in calories, saturated fat and can contain significant amounts of sugar. On top of that, during the actual manufacturing process of cleaning, fermenting and roasting the cacao beans, the natural benefits may be lost.
All in all, it seems that consuming a moderate amount of dark chocolate can’t do you harm – just look for a high cocoa solid percentage!

vocabulary.entry: dark chocolate /ˌdɑːk ˈtʃɒklət/ n. 黑巧克力
vocabulary.example: She eats a small piece of dark chocolate every day for its health benefits.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天吃一小块黑巧克力，因为它对健康有益。

vocabulary.entry: roast /rəʊst/ v. 焙炒；烘烤（食物，尤指豆类、肉类）
vocabulary.example: We roast coffee beans fresh every morning in the shop.
vocabulary.translation: 我们店里每天早上新鲜焙炒咖啡豆。

vocabulary.entry: seed /siːd/ n. 种子
vocabulary.example: The farmer planted the seed in the soil at the start of spring.
vocabulary.translation: 农民在初春时把种子播进了土壤里。

vocabulary.entry: process /prəˈses/ v. 加工；处理（原材料、食品等）
vocabulary.example: The factory processes fresh fruit into juice and jam for supermarkets.
vocabulary.translation: 这家工厂将新鲜水果加工成果汁和果酱供应超市。

vocabulary.entry: cocoa solid /ˈkəʊkəʊ ˈsɒlɪd/ n. 可可固形物
vocabulary.example: The level of cocoa solid determines the richness of dark chocolate.
vocabulary.translation: 可可固形物的含量决定了黑巧克力的浓郁度。

vocabulary.entry: cocoa butter /ˈkəʊkəʊ ˈbʌtə(r)/ n. 可可脂
vocabulary.example: Cocoa butter gives chocolate its smooth and creamy texture.
vocabulary.translation: 可可脂让巧克力拥有顺滑绵密的口感。

vocabulary.entry: dairy /ˈdeəri/ n. 乳制品；奶制食品
vocabulary.example: This chocolate contains no dairy, so it’s suitable for vegans.
vocabulary.translation: 这款巧克力不含乳制品，适合素食主义者食用。

vocabulary.entry: potential /pəˈtenʃl/ adj. 潜在的；可能的
vocabulary.example: The new drug has great potential to treat the rare disease.
vocabulary.translation: 这种新药有治疗这种罕见疾病的巨大潜力。

vocabulary.entry: cocoa content /ˈkəʊkəʊ ˈkɒntent/ n. 可可含量
vocabulary.example: Look for chocolate with a high cocoa content if you want more health benefits.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你想获得更多健康益处，就选可可含量高的巧克力。

vocabulary.entry: label /ˈleɪbl/ v. 标注；贴标签；标明
vocabulary.example: All food products must be labelled with their nutritional information.
vocabulary.translation: 所有食品都必须标注其营养成分信息。

vocabulary.entry: percentage /pəˈsentɪdʒ/ n. 百分比；百分率
vocabulary.example: The bottle is labelled with the percentage of alcohol it contains.
vocabulary.translation: 瓶子上标明了其酒精含量的百分比。

vocabulary.entry: dense /dens/ adj. 富含的；稠密的；浓密的
vocabulary.example: This type of bread is dense in fibre and very filling.
vocabulary.translation: 这种面包富含膳食纤维，饱腹感很强。

vocabulary.entry: mineral /ˈmɪnərəl/ n. 矿物质；矿物
vocabulary.example: Green leafy vegetables are a good source of essential minerals like calcium.
vocabulary.translation: 绿叶蔬菜是钙等必需矿物质的良好来源。

vocabulary.entry: magnesium /mæɡˈniːziəm/ n. 镁（一种人体必需的矿物质）
vocabulary.example: Magnesium helps to keep our muscles and nerves working properly.
vocabulary.translation: 镁有助于维持我们的肌肉和神经正常运作。

vocabulary.entry: super fruit /ˈsuːpə fruːt/ n. 超级水果（指营养价值极高的水果）
vocabulary.example: Blueberries and acai berries are often called super fruits for their high antioxidant levels.
vocabulary.translation: 蓝莓和巴西莓因其抗氧化剂含量高，常被称作超级水果。

vocabulary.entry: cranberry /ˈkrænberi/ n. 蔓越莓；蔓越橘
vocabulary.example: Cranberries are often used to make sauce to eat with turkey.
vocabulary.translation: 蔓越莓常被用来制作酱，搭配火鸡食用。

vocabulary.entry: pomegranate /ˈpɒmɪɡrænɪt/ n. 石榴

vocabulary.entry: significantly /sɪɡˈnɪfɪkəntli/ adv. 显著地；明显地；大大地

vocabulary.entry: inflammation /ˌɪnfləˈmeɪʃn/ n. 炎症；发炎
vocabulary.example: The medicine is used to reduce inflammation in the joints.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药物用于缓解关节的炎症。

vocabulary.entry: type 2 diabetes /taɪp tuː ˌdaɪəˈbiːtiːz/ n. 2型糖尿病
vocabulary.example: A healthy diet and regular exercise can help manage type 2 diabetes.
vocabulary.translation: 健康的饮食和规律的运动有助于控制2型糖尿病。

vocabulary.entry: market /ˈmɑːkɪt/ v. 推销；营销；把……推向市场

vocabulary.entry: bitter /ˈbɪtə(r)/ adj. 味苦的；苦涩的

sentences.chinese: 如果黑巧克力的可可含量（包装上以百分比标注）较高，那么它就可能富含镁、铁等矿物质。

sentences.english: According to a 2011 study comparing cacao seeds to ‘super fruits’ such as cranberries and pomegranates, dark chocolate may have high levels of antioxidants.

sentences.english: Other research includes a 2018 study which found that dark chocolate could significantly reduce inflammation in people with type 2 diabetes.

sentences.chinese: 总而言之，适量食用黑巧克力似乎不会对身体造成伤害——选购时只要认准可可固形物比例高的产品就好！

title: The alternatives to milk
paragraphs: Milk, it comes from cows, right? Well, not all the milk you see on supermarket shelves is from an udder. These days we see many plant-based alternatives to dairy, such as oat, pea and soya milk. But why would someone stop drinking their full-fat, semi-skimmed or skimmed cow’s milk and trade it for one of these?

There are many reasons someone might try alternative milks. Some people believe the alternatives are healthier than milk from cows. Those with lactose intolerance or thinking about becoming vegan might start drinking alternative milks. Also, concerns about the impact of dairy farming on the environment could be a factor. Whatever the reason, there are many alternatives to dairy out there for us to consume. But what are the differences between these other options and regular cow’s milk?

Soya milk is one common alternative. According to some sources, such as healthline.com, it contains a similar amount of protein to regular milk. It is also lower in calories than some cow’s milk, which could be good for those on a diet, and often comes fortified with things like calcium and various vitamins. So, all good? Well, soya is a common allergen, and according to foodallergy.org, is one of the nine foods which cause the majority of allergic reactions.

Almond milk is a low-calorie, low-fat drink and is naturally lactose free and has a slight nutty taste. When unsweetened, it also has lower levels of carbohydrates and sugars than some dairy options. However, even when fortified, it doesn’t provide the levels of protein seen in soya or regular milk. Then there’s coconut milk, which is low in calories and may not affect people with nut allergies as much as other options, but is lacking in protein.

Whichever plant-based milk you choose, there are positives and negatives. Dieticians agree the most important thing is getting a healthy balanced diet which won’t trigger any allergies and comes with all the minerals and vitamins you need. And at the end of the day, it may just come down to which one you think tastes better.

vocabulary.entry: plant-based /ˌplɑːnt ˈbeɪst/ adj. 以植物为基础的；植物性的
vocabulary.example: She follows a plant-based diet and doesn't eat any animal products.
vocabulary.translation: 她坚持植物性饮食，不吃任何动物制品。

vocabulary.entry: alternative /ɔːlˈtɜːnətɪv/ n. 替代品；可供选择的事物

vocabulary.translation: 现在市场上有很多乳制品的纯素替代品。

vocabulary.entry: soya /ˈsɔɪə/ n. 大豆；黄豆

vocabulary.translation: 大豆被广泛用于制作豆奶、豆腐和其他植物性食品。

vocabulary.entry: full-fat /ˌfʊl ˈfæt/ adj. 全脂的

vocabulary.entry: semi-skimmed /ˌsemi ˈskɪmd/ adj. 半脱脂的

vocabulary.entry: skimmed /skɪmd/ adj. 脱脂的

vocabulary.entry: trade /treɪd/ v. 替换；交换；以……换取

vocabulary.entry: lactose intolerance /ˈlæktəʊs ɪnˈtɒlərəns/ n. 乳糖不耐受

vocabulary.translation: 乳糖不耐受指的是身体无法正常消化牛奶中的糖分。

vocabulary.entry: vegan /ˈviːɡən/ n. 纯素主义者；严格素食主义者

vocabulary.translation: 我姐姐是纯素主义者，不吃任何动物制品。

vocabulary.entry: dairy farming /ˈdeəri ˈfɑːmɪŋ/ n. 奶牛养殖；乳制品养殖

vocabulary.translation: 在一些地区，奶牛养殖对当地环境有着较大的影响。

vocabulary.entry: consume /kənˈsjuːm/ v. 食用；饮用；消耗

vocabulary.translation: 为了获取营养，我们每周都会食用大量新鲜的果蔬。

vocabulary.entry: protein /ˈprəʊtiːn/ n. 蛋白质

vocabulary.entry: calorie /ˈkæləri/ n. 卡路里；卡（热量单位）

vocabulary.translation: 富含膳食纤维的均衡饮食对良好的消化至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: fortified /ˈfɔːtɪfaɪd/ adj. （食品）添加营养物质的；强化的

vocabulary.entry: vitamin /ˈvɪtəmɪn/ n. 维生素；维他命

sentences.english: Milk, it comes from cows, right?

sentences.english: These days we see many plant-based alternatives to dairy, such as oat, pea and soya milk.

sentences.english: But why would someone stop drinking their full-fat, semi-skimmed or skimmed cow’s milk and trade it for one of these?

sentences.chinese: 有些人认为植物奶比牛奶更健康；乳糖不耐受的人群，或是打算成为素食主义者的人，可能会开始饮用植物奶；此外，对奶牛养殖业的环境影响的担忧，也是一个可能的因素。

sentences.english: Whatever the reason, there are many alternatives to dairy out there for us to consume.

sentences.english: According to some sources, such as healthline.com, it contains a similar amount of protein to regular milk.
sentences.chinese: 据健康资讯网站Healthline等来源称，豆奶的蛋白质含量与普通牛奶相近，热量也比部分牛奶更低，很适合正在节食的人群。

sentences.english: It is also lower in calories than some cow’s milk, which could be good for those on a diet, and often comes fortified with things like calcium and various vitamins.
sentences.chinese: 而且市面上的豆奶通常会添加钙和多种维生素来强化营养。

sentences.english: So, all good?
sentences.chinese: 这么看豆奶是不是完美无缺？

sentences.english: Well, soya is a common allergen, and according to foodallergy.org, is one of the nine foods which cause the majority of allergic reactions.
sentences.chinese: 其实不然，大豆是一种常见的过敏原，据美国食品过敏研究与教育组织的数据显示，大豆是引发大多数过敏反应的九种食物之一。

sentences.english: Almond milk is a low-calorie, low-fat drink and is naturally lactose free and has a slight nutty taste.
sentences.chinese: 杏仁奶是一种低热量、低脂肪的饮品，天然不含乳糖，还带有淡淡的坚果香气。

sentences.english: When unsweetened, it also has lower levels of carbohydrates and sugars than some dairy options.
sentences.chinese: 无糖款杏仁奶的碳水化合物和糖分含量，也低于部分乳制品。

sentences.english: However, even when fortified, it doesn’t provide the levels of protein seen in soya or regular milk.
sentences.chinese: 但即便经过营养强化，杏仁奶的蛋白质含量也比不上豆奶和普通牛奶。

sentences.english: Then there’s coconut milk, which is low in calories and may not affect people with nut allergies as much as other options, but is lacking in protein.
sentences.chinese: 再来看看椰奶，它热量较低，对坚果过敏人群的影响也比其他植物奶小，但同样存在蛋白质含量不足的问题。

sentences.english: Whichever plant-based milk you choose, there are positives and negatives.
sentences.chinese: 无论你选择哪一种植物奶，它都各有优缺点。

sentences.english: Dieticians agree the most important thing is getting a healthy balanced diet which won’t trigger any allergies and comes with all the minerals and vitamins you need.
sentences.chinese: 营养师们一致认为，最重要的是保持健康均衡的饮食，这种饮食不会引发过敏，还能提供身体所需的各种矿物质和维生素。

sentences.english: And at the end of the day, it may just come down to which one you think tastes better.
sentences.chinese: 说到底，选择哪一种植物奶，可能还是取决于你觉得哪一种更好喝。

title: Rise in short-sightedness in children
paragraphs: How's your eyesight? From the moment we're born, our eyes grow, our vision becomes clearer and some of us will have normal or even 20:20 vision. However, others will become short-sighted and end up wearing glasses or contact lenses to help them see everything clearly. And some experts claim that more of us will be wearing them in the future because of our lifestyle when we were younger.

Even today, optometrists are reporting a rise in short-sightedness – also called myopia – in children. The condition can be genetic, but it's also partly being blamed on a number of modern-day factors – particularly children staring at phone screens, computers and game consoles for long periods of time. It's believed myopia also makes them susceptible to secondary eye conditions such as glaucoma, retinal detachment and other visual impairments later in life.

Of course, children have had increased screen time due to lockdowns imposed during the Covid pandemic – it's been the only way to access education and communicate with others. But education generally could be blamed for the rise in myopia. Neema Ghorbani-Mojarrad, lecturer at the University of Bradford, told BBC Future website: "We suspect it is reading and spending more time indoors. Every year of education completed increases the expected amount of short-sightedness."

The problem appears to be more severe in some Asian countries. Some experts say that in these places with huge educational success, children spend more time indoors studying. Therefore, it seems, spending more time outdoors could be good for children's eye health. The UK's College of Optometrists is suggesting parents should get their kids playing outside for two hours a day. Several scientific studies show this can prevent or stop the development of myopia.

There's been a focus on using technology, such as laser surgery, for fixing myopia, but for children at least, it seems a dose of daylight and a break from the screen might be part of the solution. Opticians also recommend kids have regular eye tests to identify any problems before they become more severe.

vocabulary.entry: eyesight /ˈaɪsaɪt/ n. 视力
vocabulary.example: Her eyesight has started to fade as she gets older.
vocabulary.translation: 随着年龄增长，她的视力开始下降。

vocabulary.entry: vision /ˈvɪʒn/ n. 视力；视觉
vocabulary.example: Poor vision can be a barrier to many daily activities.
vocabulary.translation: 视力不佳会成为很多日常活动的障碍。

vocabulary.entry: 20:20 vision /ˌtwenti ˈtwenti ˈvɪʒn/ n. 裸眼正常视力；完美视力
vocabulary.example: She has 20:20 vision and has never needed glasses.
vocabulary.translation: 她视力极好，从来不用戴眼镜。

vocabulary.entry: short-sighted /ˌʃɔːt ˈsaɪtɪd/ adj. 近视的；目光短浅的
vocabulary.example: He's been short-sighted since he was a child and wears glasses every day.
vocabulary.translation: 他从小就近视，每天都要戴眼镜。

vocabulary.entry: contact lens /ˈkɒntækt lens/ n. 隐形眼镜
vocabulary.example: I prefer wearing contact lenses to glasses when I play sports.
vocabulary.translation: 我运动时更喜欢戴隐形眼镜而不是框架眼镜。

vocabulary.entry: expert /ˈekspɜːt/ n. 专家；能手 adj. 专业的；熟练的
vocabulary.example: She's an expert in child psychology.
vocabulary.translation: 她是儿童心理学方面的专家。

vocabulary.entry: optometrist /ɒpˈtɒmətrɪst/ n. 验光师；视光师
vocabulary.example: You should see an optometrist at least once a year to check your eyes.
vocabulary.translation: 你应该每年至少看一次验光师检查视力。

vocabulary.entry: myopia /maɪˈəʊpiə/ n. 近视（医学术语）
vocabulary.example: The study focuses on the causes of juvenile myopia in children.
vocabulary.translation: 这项研究聚焦于儿童青少年近视的成因。

vocabulary.entry: genetic /dʒəˈnetɪk/ adj. 基因的；遗传的
vocabulary.example: Some forms of eye disease are genetic and run in families.
vocabulary.translation: 有些眼病是遗传性的，会在家族中遗传。

vocabulary.entry: modern-day /ˌmɒdn ˈdeɪ/ adj. 现代的；当代的
vocabulary.example: Social media is a modern-day phenomenon that has changed how we communicate.
vocabulary.translation: 社交媒体是一种现代现象，改变了我们的沟通方式。

vocabulary.entry: game console /ˈɡeɪm kənˈsəʊl/ n. 游戏机
vocabulary.example: He spent the weekend playing video games on his new game console.
vocabulary.translation: 他整个周末都在新游戏机上玩电子游戏。

vocabulary.entry: susceptible /səˈseptəbl/ adj. 易患（病）的；易受影响的
vocabulary.example: People with weak immune systems are more susceptible to infections.
vocabulary.translation: 免疫系统薄弱的人更容易感染疾病。

vocabulary.entry: secondary /ˈsekəndəri/ adj. 继发性的；次要的
vocabulary.example: The patient developed a secondary infection after the initial illness.
vocabulary.translation: 这位病人在原发疾病后出现了继发性感染。

vocabulary.entry: glaucoma /ɡləʊˈkəʊmə/ n. 青光眼（眼科疾病）
vocabulary.example: Glaucoma can cause permanent vision loss if it's not treated early.
vocabulary.translation: 青光眼如果不及早治疗，可能会导致永久性视力丧失。

vocabulary.entry: retinal /ˈretɪnl/ adj. 视网膜的
vocabulary.example: The doctor diagnosed her with a retinal problem that needed urgent treatment.
vocabulary.translation: 医生诊断她患有视网膜疾病，需要紧急治疗。

vocabulary.entry: detachment /dɪˈtætʃmənt/ n. 脱离；分离
vocabulary.example: Retinal detachment is a serious eye condition that requires immediate surgery.
vocabulary.translation: 视网膜脱离是一种严重的眼科疾病，需要立即做手术。

vocabulary.entry: visual impairment /ˈvɪʒuəl ɪmˈpeəmənt/ n. 视力损伤；视力障碍
vocabulary.example: The charity provides support for people with visual impairment of all levels.
vocabulary.translation: 这家慈善机构为不同程度的视力障碍者提供帮助。

vocabulary.entry: lockdown /ˈlɒkdaʊn/ n. 封控；封锁
vocabulary.example: Many people worked from home during the lockdown to stop the spread of the virus.
vocabulary.translation: 封控期间，很多人为了阻止病毒传播选择居家办公。

vocabulary.entry: impose /ɪmˈpəʊz/ v. 实施；强加
vocabulary.example: The government decided to impose new rules to limit public gatherings.
vocabulary.translation: 政府决定实施新规限制公众聚集。

vocabulary.entry: access /ˈækses/ v. 获取；使用 n. 通道；使用权
vocabulary.example: Students can access online learning resources at any time.
vocabulary.translation: 学生可以随时获取在线学习资源。

vocabulary.entry: indoors /ˌɪnˈdɔːz/ adv. 在室内；进入室内 n. 室内
vocabulary.example: We spent the whole day indoors because of the heavy rain.
vocabulary.translation: 因为下大雨，我们一整天都待在室内。

vocabulary.entry: severe /sɪˈvɪə(r)/ adj. 严重的；剧烈的
vocabulary.example: The region suffered a severe drought that lasted for six months.
vocabulary.translation: 该地区遭遇了持续六个月的严重干旱。

vocabulary.entry: laser surgery /ˈleɪzə ˈsɜːdʒəri/ n. 激光手术
vocabulary.example: Many people choose laser surgery to correct their myopia and avoid wearing glasses.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人选择激光手术矫正近视，摆脱戴眼镜的困扰。

vocabulary.entry: fix /fɪks/ v. 矫正；修复；解决
vocabulary.example: This surgery can fix certain eye problems and improve vision.
vocabulary.translation: 这种手术可以矫正某些眼部问题，改善视力。

vocabulary.entry: optician /ɒpˈtɪʃn/ n. 配镜师；眼镜商
vocabulary.example: The optician helped me choose a new pair of glasses that suit my face.
vocabulary.translation: 配镜师帮我选了一副适合我脸型的新眼镜。

sentences.english: How's your eyesight?
sentences.chinese: 你的视力怎么样？

sentences.english: From the moment we're born, our eyes grow, our vision becomes clearer and some of us will have normal or even 20:20 vision.
sentences.chinese: 从出生的那一刻起，我们的眼睛就会不断发育，视力会变得越来越清晰，有些人会拥有正常甚至是2.0的视力。

sentences.english: However, others will become short-sighted and end up wearing glasses or contact lenses to help them see everything clearly.
sentences.chinese: 但另一些人则会患上近视，最终需要戴上眼镜或隐形眼镜才能看清事物。

sentences.english: And some experts claim that more of us will be wearing them in the future because of our lifestyle when we were younger.
sentences.chinese: 一些专家称，由于我们年轻时的生活方式，未来会有更多人需要佩戴矫正视力的眼镜。

sentences.english: Even today, optometrists are reporting a rise in short-sightedness – also called myopia – in children.
sentences.chinese: 即便是现在，验光师们也指出儿童患近视眼的比率正在上升。

sentences.english: The condition can be genetic, but it's also partly being blamed on a number of modern-day factors – particularly children staring at phone screens, computers and game consoles for long periods of time.
sentences.chinese: 近视可能与遗传有关，但也有部分原因要归咎于多种现代因素——尤其是儿童长时间盯着手机屏幕、电脑和游戏机。

sentences.english: It's believed myopia also makes them susceptible to secondary eye conditions such as glaucoma, retinal detachment and other visual impairments later in life.
sentences.chinese: 有观点认为，近视还会让他们在日后更容易患上继发性眼部疾病，比如青光眼、视网膜脱落以及其他视力损伤问题。

sentences.english: Of course, children have had increased screen time due to lockdowns imposed during the Covid pandemic – it's been the only way to access education and communicate with others.
sentences.chinese: 当然，新冠疫情期间的封锁措施导致儿童的屏幕使用时间有所增加——这曾是他们接受教育和与他人沟通的唯一途径。

title: Ice cream innovation
paragraphs: Is there anything nicer than a cooling ice cream on a hot summer's day? This traditional treat is centuries old, but our tastes and consumer habits are evolving. How is the ice cream production process changing, and who is driving this change?

Making ice cream is a time-consuming process. While the recipe is simple – milk, sugar and fat, plus flavours and colours – ice cream has a complex chemistry. Getting the balance right between ice, fat and air is important if the ice cream is to have the right texture. To achieve this, the ingredients need to be mixed and heated, then cooled and frozen – a process that takes time and uses a lot of energy. Designers and engineers are working to improve the production process with new specialised equipment to make it increasingly automated. For now, however, even with the help of robots and 3D printers, it can take up to two years from testing a new frozen dessert product to it being available to consumers.

And demand is only going up. According to the food packaging company Tetra Pak, more than 25 billion litres of ice cream were eaten worldwide in 2021. While the US and China are the biggest consumers, data from NielsenIQ shows that people in the UK bought 28% more ice cream during the UK's record-breaking summer compared to a year earlier. Clearly, rising temperatures can explain why some people are buying more ice cream, but it's not the only explanation. The pandemic has seen people reaching for pleasures they can enjoy at home, which include eating indulgent foods. And worries about the cost-of-living crisis could have a similar effect, as even a premium ice cream is an affordable treat.

So, what new things can we expect on a stick or in a cone? Consumers of all ages buy ice cream, but it is millennial consumers who are driving interest in more original flavours, including spices. Dairy still dominates, but plant-based ice cream, sorbets and low-calorie choices are a growing part of the frozen dessert market. But, according to Elsebeth Baungaard, portfolio manager at Tetra Pak, the next global trend will be less about innovation and more about portion size. "I'm sorry to say it's simply shrinking", she says. "But the quality will be higher."

title: Are we born to love learning
paragraphs: Are you the kind of person who hated school? Or are you more like Michael Nicholson, who can't stop learning? He currently has 30 degrees including 22 master's and a doctorate! If you're also passionate about studying, you might be a philomath – a person who loves to learn and study. The word comes from Greek with 'phil' meaning 'a lover of' and 'math' meaning 'learning'.

Humans are all philomaths to an extent – our brain is hardwired to be curious. We want to learn and understand, partly to make sense of the world but also because of something called neoteny. This is a term that refers to the juvenile characteristics of some animals, including humans, being retained into adulthood. One of these traits is neuroplasticity, which helps our brains stay flexible – this gives us the ability to learn throughout our lives. Many creatures which are genetically close to us, like primates, can't do this and only learn during their adolescence.

But for every person who loves learning, there are plenty who can't stand it. Lots of people remember their school days as being boring or even pointless. Why is this? Educational anthropologists have suggested that if a concept or idea is too complex or dull, it becomes harder to link old and new ideas together. If that's the case, we lose motivation and absorb less information. This negative experience of education at school may lead to people avoiding learning opportunities in later life.

So, don't let a bad educational experience prevent you learning something new as an adult. Evolution has made us lifelong learners, so take advantage of your biology and discover your inner philomath. Who knows what you could achieve?

vocabulary.translation: 人类在基因上与黑猩猩和其他类人猿关系密切。

vocabulary.entry: primate /ˈpraɪmeɪt/ n. 灵长目动物
vocabulary.example: Monkeys, apes and humans are all primates.
vocabulary.translation: 猴子、猿类和人类都是灵长目动物。

vocabulary.entry: adolescence /ˌædəˈlesns/ n. 青春期；青少年时期
vocabulary.example: Adolescence is a period of great physical and emotional change for young people.
vocabulary.translation: 青春期是年轻人身心发生巨大变化的时期。

vocabulary.entry: stand /stænd/ v. 忍受；承受；容忍（常用于否定句/疑问句）
vocabulary.example: I can't stand the noise from the construction site next door.
vocabulary.translation: 我受不了隔壁建筑工地的噪音。

vocabulary.entry: educational anthropologist /ˌedʒuˈkeɪʃənl ˌænθrəˈpɒlədʒɪst/ n. 教育人类学家
vocabulary.example: The educational anthropologist studied how culture influences children's learning.
vocabulary.translation: 这位教育人类学家研究了文化如何影响儿童的学习。

vocabulary.entry: concept /ˈkɒnsept/ n. 概念；观念；理念
vocabulary.example: It's difficult for young children to understand the concept of time.
vocabulary.translation: 小孩子很难理解时间的概念。

vocabulary.entry: complex /ˈkɒmpleks/ adj. 复杂的；难懂的；错综的 n. 综合体
vocabulary.example: The book explains complex scientific ideas in simple language.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书用简单的语言解释了复杂的科学概念。

vocabulary.entry: dull /dʌl/ adj. 枯燥的；乏味的；无趣的；迟钝的
vocabulary.example: Many students find history lessons dull if they are taught just by reading textbooks.
vocabulary.translation: 如果历史课只靠读课本讲授，很多学生会觉得枯燥。

vocabulary.entry: link /lɪŋk/ v. 连接；关联；把……联系起来 n. 联系；纽带
vocabulary.example: We need to link the new knowledge with what we have learned before.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要把新知识和之前学过的内容联系起来。

vocabulary.entry: motivation /ˌməʊtɪˈveɪʃn/ n. 学习动力；积极性；动机；原因
vocabulary.example: The teacher tries to boost students' motivation by using interesting teaching methods.
vocabulary.translation: 这位老师通过有趣的教学方法努力调动学生的学习积极性。

vocabulary.entry: absorb /əbˈsɔːb/ v. 吸收（知识、信息）；理解；掌握；吸收（物质）
vocabulary.example: Children absorb new language skills much faster than adults.
vocabulary.translation: 儿童吸收新的语言技能比成年人快得多。

vocabulary.entry: prevent /prɪˈvent/ v. 阻止；阻碍；防止；使不能发生
vocabulary.example: Fear of failure should not prevent you from trying new things.
vocabulary.translation: 对失败的恐惧不应阻碍你尝试新事物。

vocabulary.entry: evolution /ˌiːvəˈluːʃn/ n. 进化；演化；发展；演变
vocabulary.example: The theory of evolution was put forward by Charles Darwin.
vocabulary.translation: 进化论是由查尔斯·达尔文提出的。

vocabulary.entry: biology /baɪˈɒlədʒi/ n. 生物学；（人体的）生理机能；生物构造
vocabulary.example: Human biology allows us to be lifelong learners if we make the most of it.
vocabulary.translation: 人类的生理构造让我们能成为终身学习者，只要我们充分利用这一点。

vocabulary.entry: inner /ˈɪnə(r)/ adj. 内心的；内在的；深藏的；核心的
vocabulary.example: She found her inner strength to face the difficulties in her life.
vocabulary.translation: 她找到了面对生活困境的内心力量。

sentences.english: Are you the kind of person who hated school?
sentences.chinese: 你是那种讨厌上学的人吗？

sentences.english: Or are you more like Michael Nicholson, who can't stop learning?
sentences.chinese: 还是说，你更像迈克尔·尼科尔森无法停止学习？

sentences.english: He currently has 30 degrees including 22 master's and a doctorate!
sentences.chinese: 他目前拥有30个学位，其中包括22个硕士学位和1个博士学位！

sentences.english: If you're also passionate about studying, you might be a philomath – a person who loves to learn and study.
sentences.chinese: 如果你同样热衷于学习，那你可能就是一名“爱学者”——指热爱学习和钻研的人。

sentences.english: The word comes from Greek with 'phil' meaning 'a lover of' and 'math' meaning 'learning'.
sentences.chinese: 这个词源于希腊语，“phil”意为“热爱……的人”，“math”则表示“学习”。

sentences.english: Humans are all philomaths to an extent – our brain is hardwired to be curious.
sentences.chinese: 从某种程度上来说，人类都是热爱学习的人——我们的大脑天生就具备好奇心。

sentences.english: We want to learn and understand, partly to make sense of the world but also because of something called neoteny.
sentences.chinese: 我们渴望学习和理解事物，一部分是为了认清世界的运行规律，另一部分则是源于一种名为“幼态延续”的现象。

sentences.english: This is a term that refers to the juvenile characteristics of some animals, including humans, being retained into adulthood.
sentences.chinese: 这个术语指的是部分动物（包括人类）在成年后依然保留着幼年时期的特征。

sentences.english: One of these traits is neuroplasticity, which helps our brains stay flexible – this gives us the ability to learn throughout our lives.
sentences.chinese: 其中一项特征就是神经可塑性，它能让我们的大脑保持灵活，让我们拥有终身学习的能力。

sentences.english: Many creatures which are genetically close to us, like primates, can't do this and only learn during their adolescence.
sentences.chinese: 许多和我们基因相近的生物，比如灵长类动物，就不具备这种能力，它们的学习能力只存在于青春期。

sentences.english: But for every person who loves learning, there are plenty who can't stand it.
sentences.chinese: 不过，有多少人热爱学习，就有多少人对学习深恶痛绝。

sentences.english: Lots of people remember their school days as being boring or even pointless.
sentences.chinese: 很多人回忆起学生时代，都觉得那段时光枯燥乏味，甚至毫无意义。

sentences.english: Why is this?
sentences.chinese: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.english: Educational anthropologists have suggested that if a concept or idea is too complex or dull, it becomes harder to link old and new ideas together.
sentences.chinese: 教育人类学家指出，如果某个概念或知识点过于复杂、乏味，人们就很难将新旧知识串联起来。

sentences.english: If that's the case, we lose motivation and absorb less information.
sentences.chinese: 一旦出现这种情况，我们就会失去学习动力，吸收的知识也会大打折扣。

sentences.english: This negative experience of education at school may lead to people avoiding learning opportunities in later life.
sentences.chinese: 这种糟糕的校园学习经历，可能会导致人们在成年后刻意回避学习的机会。

sentences.english: So, don't let a bad educational experience prevent you learning something new as an adult.
sentences.chinese: 所以，不要让一段糟糕的求学经历，阻碍你在成年后学习新事物的脚步。

sentences.english: Evolution has made us lifelong learners, so take advantage of your biology and discover your inner philomath.
sentences.chinese: 进化让我们成为了终身学习者，所以请好好利用自身的生理优势，发掘内心深处那个热爱学习的自己吧。

sentences.english: Who knows what you could achieve?
sentences.chinese: 谁知道你能取得怎样的成就呢？

title: Controlling the weather
paragraphs: The weather affects all of us. An unexpected downpour or hot spell can be annoying, but when conditions are more extreme, it can severely impact agriculture, transport infrastructure and our homes. It's no surprise that for centuries scientists have tried to control the weather – but is it really possible?

Due to climate change, there are more regular occurrences of heatwaves, which cause droughts, and torrential rain, which is responsible for flooding. Although humans are the cause of much of it, maybe we have a solution too? For example, China, the UAE and the USA are at the forefront of research into methods of producing rain in drought-stricken areas. And some scientists are even thinking about investigating technologies which could cool the entire planet.

It might sound like science fiction, but weather modification is nothing new. In the 1940s, scientists discovered that dropping particles of silver iodide into cloud tops, made the tiny water droplets condense and could stimulate precipitation. That's called cloud seeding. This is a technique still being tested today with the aim of producing extra rainfall and, therefore, water for drought-affected farmers.

Other ideas for keeping nature at bay include using lasers to generate clouds and for controlling thunderstorms. One idea involved firing laser pulses into thunderclouds in an attempt to suck out lightning in a controlled manner. This was unsuccessful. New research into solar geoengineering has also begun. This type of climate engineering involves sunlight being reflected back to space to limit or reverse human-caused climate change.

Despite all this ongoing research, there's no conclusive evidence that our weather can be controlled. Chris Bell, a lecturer in meteorology at the University of East Anglia, told BBC Future: "We may, one day, have the technology to control the weather, but it will be in thousands, not hundreds, of years." So, for now, we still need to rely on Mother Nature to control our weather.

vocabulary.entry: downpour /ˈdaʊnpɔː(r)/ n. 暴雨；倾盆大雨
vocabulary.example: We were caught in a sudden downpour on the way home.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在回家的路上遇上了突如其来的暴雨。

vocabulary.entry: hot spell /hɒt spel/ n. 持续高温期；酷暑
vocabulary.example: The country is experiencing a long hot spell with temperatures over 35℃.
vocabulary.translation: 这个国家正遭遇持续的酷暑，气温超过35摄氏度。

vocabulary.entry: extreme /ɪkˈstriːm/ adj. （天气、情况）极端的；极度的
vocabulary.example: Extreme weather conditions have disrupted air travel across the country.
vocabulary.translation: 极端天气状况打乱了全国的航空出行。

vocabulary.entry: agriculture /ˈæɡrɪkʌltʃə(r)/ n. 农业；农学；农艺
vocabulary.example: The region's economy is largely based on agriculture and fishing.
vocabulary.translation: 这个地区的经济主要以农业和渔业为基础。

vocabulary.entry: transport infrastructure /ˈtrænspɔːt ˈɪnfrəstrʌktʃə(r)/ n. 交通基础设施
vocabulary.example: The government is investing in new transport infrastructure to improve connectivity.
vocabulary.translation: 政府正投资建设新的交通基础设施，以提升互联互通性。

vocabulary.entry: occurrence /əˈkʌrəns/ n. 发生；出现；（偶发的）事件
vocabulary.example: There has been an increase in the occurrence of forest fires in recent years.
vocabulary.translation: 近年来森林火灾的发生频次有所上升。

vocabulary.entry: heatwave /ˈhiːtweɪv/ n. 热浪；持续高温天气
vocabulary.example: The heatwave led to a sharp rise in demand for electricity for air conditioning.
vocabulary.translation: 这场热浪导致空调用电需求急剧上升。

vocabulary.entry: drought /draʊt/ n. 干旱；旱灾；缺水期
vocabulary.example: The long drought has ruined the crops in the local farmland.
vocabulary.translation: 长期的干旱毁掉了当地农田里的庄稼。

vocabulary.entry: torrential /təˈrenʃl/ adj. （雨）倾盆的；暴雨的；倾泻的
vocabulary.example: Torrential rain caused rivers to overflow and roads to close.
vocabulary.translation: 暴雨导致河水泛滥、道路封闭。

vocabulary.entry: flooding /ˈflʌdɪŋ/ n. 洪水；泛滥；水淹
vocabulary.example: Flooding in the valley has forced hundreds of people to leave their homes.
vocabulary.translation: 山谷的洪水迫使数百人离开家园。

vocabulary.entry: at the forefront /æt ðə ˈfɔːfrʌnt/ 处于前沿；在首位；成为领军者
vocabulary.example: This company is at the forefront of research into renewable energy.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司在可再生能源的研究领域处于前沿地位。

vocabulary.entry: drought-stricken /ˌdraʊt ˈstrɪkən/ adj. 遭受干旱的；受旱灾影响的
vocabulary.example: Charities are sending water and food to drought-stricken areas in the south.
vocabulary.translation: 慈善机构正为南部受旱灾影响的地区运送水和食物。

vocabulary.entry: investigate /ɪnˈvestɪɡeɪt/ v. 调查；研究；探究（未知事物）
vocabulary.example: Scientists are investigating new ways to treat the rare disease.
vocabulary.translation: 科学家们正在研究治疗这种罕见疾病的新方法。

vocabulary.entry: weather modification /ˈweðə ˌmɒdɪfɪˈkeɪʃn/ n. 人工影响天气；天气改造
vocabulary.example: Many countries are researching weather modification to deal with extreme climate.
vocabulary.translation: 许多国家都在研究人工影响天气技术，以应对极端气候。

vocabulary.entry: silver iodide /ˈsɪlvə ˈaɪədaɪd/ n. 碘化银（化学物质，用于人工增雨）
vocabulary.example: Silver iodide is a common chemical used in cloud seeding operations.
vocabulary.translation: 碘化银是人工增雨作业中常用的化学物质。

vocabulary.entry: droplet /ˈdrɒplət/ n. 小水滴；小液滴
vocabulary.example: Water droplets on the window froze in the cold weather.
vocabulary.translation: 窗户上的小水滴在寒冷的天气里结冰了。

vocabulary.entry: condense /kənˈdens/ v. （气体、蒸汽）凝结；浓缩
vocabulary.example: Warm moist air condenses into clouds when it meets cold air.
vocabulary.translation: 温暖的湿空气遇到冷空气就会凝结成云。

vocabulary.entry: stimulate /ˈstɪmjuleɪt/ v. 促进；激发；刺激（发生、产生）
vocabulary.example: The chemical is used to stimulate plant growth in cold climates.
vocabulary.translation: 这种化学物质用于在寒冷气候中促进植物生长。

vocabulary.entry: precipitation /prɪˌsɪpɪˈteɪʃn/ n. 降水；降雨量（雨、雪、冰雹等的统称）
vocabulary.example: Annual precipitation in this desert area is less than 50 millimetres.
vocabulary.translation: 这个沙漠地区的年降水量不足50毫米。

vocabulary.entry: cloud seeding /klaʊd ˈsiːdɪŋ/ n. 人工增雨；云催化
vocabulary.example: Cloud seeding has been used to increase rainfall in some drought-affected regions.
vocabulary.translation: 人工增雨技术已被用于为一些受干旱影响的地区增加降雨量。

vocabulary.entry: technique /tekˈniːk/ n. 技术；工艺；方法；技巧
vocabulary.example: The doctor developed a new technique for treating heart disease.
vocabulary.translation: 这位医生研发出了一种治疗心脏病的新技术。

vocabulary.entry: keep nature at bay /kiːp ˈneɪtʃə æt beɪ/ 抵御自然力量；阻止自然灾害发生；防范大自然的威胁
vocabulary.example: We build sea walls to keep the sea at bay and prevent flooding.
vocabulary.translation: 我们修建海堤来抵御海水，防止洪水泛滥。

vocabulary.entry: laser /ˈleɪzə(r)/ n. 激光；激光器
vocabulary.example: Lasers are widely used in medicine, industry and communication.
vocabulary.translation: 激光被广泛应用于医疗、工业和通信领域。

vocabulary.entry: generate /ˈdʒenəreɪt/ v. 产生；生成；创造
vocabulary.example: The machine is designed to generate electricity from wind power.
vocabulary.translation: 这款机器的设计原理是利用风能发电。

vocabulary.entry: thunderstorm /ˈθʌndəstɔːm/ n. 雷雨；雷暴（天气）
vocabulary.example: A severe thunderstorm hit the city last night, bringing strong winds and hail.
vocabulary.translation: 昨晚一场强雷暴袭击了这座城市，带来了狂风和冰雹。

vocabulary.entry: pulse /pʌls/ n. （光、电、声的）脉冲；搏动
vocabulary.example: The laser emits short pulses of light that can cut through metal.
vocabulary.translation: 这台激光器发射的短光脉冲可以切割金属。

vocabulary.entry: thundercloud /ˈθʌndəklaʊd/ n. 雷雨云；积雨云
vocabulary.example: Black thunderclouds gathered overhead, and we knew a storm was coming.
vocabulary.translation: 头顶聚起了黑压压的雷雨云，我们知道暴风雨要来了。

vocabulary.entry: suck out /sʌk aʊt/ 吸出；抽走；提取
vocabulary.example: The machine can suck out water from the flooded basement quickly.
vocabulary.translation: 这台机器能快速从被水淹的地下室抽水。

vocabulary.entry: lightning /ˈlaɪtnɪŋ/ n. 闪电；雷电
vocabulary.example: A flash of lightning lit up the sky, followed by a loud clap of thunder.
vocabulary.translation: 一道闪电划破天空，接着是一声巨响的雷鸣。

vocabulary.entry: solar geoengineering /ˈsəʊlə dʒiːəʊendʒɪˈnɪərɪŋ/ n. 太阳能地球工程；太阳辐射管理
vocabulary.example: Scientists are debating the risks and benefits of solar geoengineering to cool the planet.
vocabulary.translation: 科学家们正在争论太阳能地球工程为地球降温的利弊。

vocabulary.entry: climate engineering /ˈklaɪmət ˌendʒɪˈnɪərɪŋ/ n. 气候工程
vocabulary.example: Climate engineering is a controversial field that aims to manipulate the global climate.
vocabulary.translation: 气候工程是一个颇具争议的领域，其目的是人为干预全球气候。

vocabulary.entry: reflect /rɪˈflekt/ v. （光、热、声音）反射；映照
vocabulary.example: The white sand reflects the sun's rays and makes the beach very bright.
vocabulary.translation: 白色的沙子反射阳光，让海滩变得格外明亮。

vocabulary.entry: reverse /rɪˈvɜːs/ v. 逆转；反转；扭转（趋势、结果）
vocabulary.example: We need to take action to reverse the damage caused by climate change.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要采取行动，扭转气候变化造成的破坏。

vocabulary.entry: ongoing /ˈɒnɡəʊɪŋ/ adj. 正在进行的；持续的；未完成的
vocabulary.example: There is an ongoing investigation into the cause of the plane crash.
vocabulary.translation: 对这起飞机失事原因的调查正在进行中。

vocabulary.entry: conclusive /kənˈkluːsɪv/ adj. 确凿的；结论性的；决定性的
vocabulary.example: There is no conclusive evidence to prove that he is guilty of the crime.
vocabulary.translation: 目前没有确凿的证据证明他犯有这项罪行。

vocabulary.entry: meteorology /ˌmiːtiəˈrɒlədʒi/ n. 气象学；气象状态
vocabulary.example: She studied meteorology at university and now works as a weather forecaster.
vocabulary.translation: 她在大学里学的是气象学，现在担任天气预报员。

vocabulary.entry: rely on /rɪˈlaɪ ɒn/ 依靠；依赖；信赖
vocabulary.example: Many small businesses rely on government support to survive the economic crisis.
vocabulary.translation: 许多小企业依靠政府扶持度过经济危机。

vocabulary.entry: Mother Nature /ˈmʌðə ˈneɪtʃə/ n. 大自然；自然界（拟人化表达）
vocabulary.example: We need to respect Mother Nature and protect the environment around us.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要敬畏大自然，保护身边的环境。

sentences.english: In the 1940s, scientists discovered that dropping particles of silver iodide into cloud tops, made the tiny water droplets condense and could stimulate precipitation.
sentences.chinese: 20世纪40年代，科学家们发现，将碘化银颗粒撒入云层顶部，能够促使微小的水滴凝结，进而形成降水。

sentences.english: That's called cloud seeding.
sentences.chinese: 这种方法被称为人工增雨。

sentences.english: This is a technique still being tested today with the aim of producing extra rainfall and, therefore, water for drought-affected farmers.
sentences.chinese: 如今这项技术仍在试验阶段，其目的是增加降雨量，从而为受干旱影响的农民提供水源。

sentences.english: Other ideas for keeping nature at bay include using lasers to generate clouds and for controlling thunderstorms.
sentences.chinese: 其他抵御极端天气的构想还包括利用激光造云以及控制雷暴。

sentences.english: One idea involved firing laser pulses into thunderclouds in an attempt to suck out lightning in a controlled manner. This was unsuccessful.
sentences.chinese: 有一个构想是向雷雨云发射激光脉冲，试图以可控的方式引导闪电释放，但这个尝试并未成功。

sentences.english: New research into solar geoengineering has also begun. This type of climate engineering involves sunlight being reflected back to space to limit or reverse human-caused climate change.
sentences.chinese: 太阳能地球工程的相关研究也已启动，这类气候工程技术旨在将太阳光反射回太空，从而限制或逆转人类活动引发的气候变化。

sentences.english: Despite all this ongoing research, there's no conclusive evidence that our weather can be controlled.
sentences.chinese: 尽管相关研究一直在进行，但目前尚无确凿证据表明人类能够控制天气。

sentences.english: Chris Bell, a lecturer in meteorology at the University of East Anglia, told BBC Future: "We may, one day, have the technology to control the weather, but it will be in thousands, not hundreds, of years."
sentences.chinese: 东安格利亚大学的气象学讲师克里斯·贝尔在接受BBC未来频道采访时表示：“或许有一天，我们会掌握控制天气的技术，但这需要数千年的时间，而非几百年。”

sentences.english: So, for now, we still need to rely on Mother Nature to control our weather.
sentences.chinese: 因此，目前仍然是大自然掌控天气。

title: Are first impressions really accurate
titleChinese: 人们对他人的第一印象是否准确？
paragraphs: Are you a good judge of character? Can you make an accurate judgement of someone's personality based only on your first impression of them? Ironically, the answer lies as much in them as it does in you.

One of the first people to try to identify good judges of character was US psychologist Henry F Adams in 1927. His research led him to conclude that people fell into two groups – good judges of themselves and good judges of others. Adams's research has been widely criticised since then, but he wasn't entirely wrong about there being two distinct types.

More on that in a moment, but first we need to define what a good judge of character is. Is it someone who can read personality or someone who can read emotion? Those are two distinct skills. Emotions such as anger or joy or sadness can generate easily identifiable physical signs. Most of us would probably be able to accurately identify these signs, even in a stranger. As such, most of us are probably good judges of emotion.

In order to be a good judge of personality, however, there needs to be an interaction with the other person, and that person needs to be a 'good target'. 'Good targets' are people who reveal relevant and useful cues to their personality. So this means 'the good judge' will only manifest when reading 'good targets'. This is according to Rogers and Biesanz in their 2019 journal entitled 'Reassessing the good judge of personality'. "We found consistent, clear and strong evidence that the good judge does exist", Rogers and Biesanz concluded. But their key finding is that the good judge does not have magical gifts of perception – they are simply able to "detect and utilise information provided by the good target".

So, are first impressions really accurate? Well, if you're a good judge talking to a 'good target', then it seems the answer is 'yes'. And now we know that good judges probably do exist, more research can be done into how they read personality, what kind of people they are – and whether their skills can be taught.

title: Should you build a capsule wardrobe
titleChinese: 你可能也需要一个“胶囊衣橱”
paragraphs: Do you ever struggle with choosing your outfit in the morning? If you have a full wardrobe yet still feel you don't have anything to wear, you might want to build yourself a capsule wardrobe!

So, what is this? Put simply, a capsule wardrobe is a small selection of items of clothing that complement each other, and are therefore interchangeable. Key to the capsule wardrobe is solid basics, like plain tops, and, ideally, neutral colours, because they make combinations easier. Think about the versatility of a simple pair of denim jeans. They can be combined with trainers and a t-shirt for a casual look or a blazer paired with heels, or loafers, if you want to look more sophisticated. Fashion bloggers also talk about timeless classics – picture a luxury black handbag that will suit any occasion and won't go out of style.

But why might it be beneficial to build a capsule wardrobe? Well, by limiting your choices, it can become much easier to choose what to wear, but there is another advantage too – it can reduce the amount of fast fashion. Fast fashion refers to clothes which are trendy for just a short time, so are quickly replaced by newer trends. This results in cheap and poor-quality clothing which has huge environmental costs as waste goes to landfill, resulting in an increase in pollution. According to UK clothes waste charity TRAID, the average garment is worn just 10 times before being disposed of. So, having a capsule wardrobe with long-lasting and high-quality clothes should help reduce this, even if it means paying more in the first place.

Fashion and lifestyle magazine, Vogue, says 'building an excellent capsule wardrobe takes time and patience'. But, if you want to reduce waste and have some extra time in the morning, it might be time to start building!

vocabulary.translation: 她买了一条高端皮质腰带，能用很多年。

vocabulary.entry: go out of style /ɡəʊ aʊt ɒv staɪl/ 过时；不再流行

vocabulary.translation: 无论潮流如何，经典设计永远不会过时。

vocabulary.translation: 吃新鲜水果对你的消化系统有益。

vocabulary.translation: 以环保的方式处理旧衣物十分重要。

vocabulary.entry: long-lasting /ˌlɒŋ ˈlɑːstɪŋ/ adj. （衣物）耐用的；持久的

vocabulary.entry: in the first place /ɪn ðə fɜːst pleɪs/ 起初；一开始

sentences.english: Do you ever struggle with choosing your outfit in the morning?

sentences.english: If you have a full wardrobe yet still feel you don't have anything to wear, you might want to build yourself a capsule wardrobe!
sentences.chinese: 要是你的衣柜明明满满当当，却依然觉得没衣服可穿，那或许你该给自己打造一个胶囊衣橱了！

sentences.english: So, what is this?
sentences.chinese: 那么，什么是胶囊衣橱呢？

sentences.chinese: 简单来说，胶囊衣橱就是一小部分相互搭配、可以灵活组合的衣物。

sentences.english: Key to the capsule wardrobe is solid basics, like plain tops, and, ideally, neutral colours, because they make combinations easier.
sentences.chinese: 胶囊衣橱的核心是基础款单品，比如纯色上衣，而且最好是中性色系，因为这类颜色更容易搭配。

sentences.english: Think about the versatility of a simple pair of denim jeans. They can be combined with trainers and a t-shirt for a casual look or a blazer paired with heels, or loafers, if you want to look more sophisticated.
sentences.chinese: 想想一条简约牛仔裤的百搭性：搭配运动鞋和T恤，就是一身休闲装扮；要是想穿得更精致些，配上西装外套和高跟鞋或乐福鞋就好。

sentences.english: Fashion bloggers also talk about timeless classics – picture a luxury black handbag that will suit any occasion and won't go out of style.
sentences.chinese: 时尚博主们还会提到永不过时的经典款——比如一只质感高级的黑色手提包，它适配各种场合，而且永远不会过时。

sentences.english: But why might it be beneficial to build a capsule wardrobe?
sentences.chinese: 不过，打造胶囊衣橱到底有什么好处呢？

sentences.english: Well, by limiting your choices, it can become much easier to choose what to wear, but there is another advantage too – it can reduce the amount of fast fashion.
sentences.chinese: 首先，精简衣物选择后，早上挑衣服会变得轻松很多；其次，它还能减少快时尚的消费。

sentences.english: Fast fashion refers to clothes which are trendy for just a short time, so are quickly replaced by newer trends.
sentences.chinese: 快时尚指的是那些只流行很短时间、很快就会被新潮流取代的服装。

sentences.english: This results in cheap and poor-quality clothing which has huge environmental costs as waste goes to landfill, resulting in an increase in pollution.
sentences.chinese: 这类价格低廉、质量较差的衣物被当做垃圾送往填埋场，会造成严重的环境污染。

sentences.english: According to UK clothes waste charity TRAID, the average garment is worn just 10 times before being disposed of.
sentences.chinese: 英国衣物回收慈善机构TRAID的数据显示，一件衣服平均只被穿10次就会被丢弃。

sentences.english: So, having a capsule wardrobe with long-lasting and high-quality clothes should help reduce this, even if it means paying more in the first place.
sentences.chinese: 因此，拥有一个由耐穿、高品质衣物组成的胶囊衣橱，即便初期投入更高，也有助于减少这种浪费现象。

sentences.english: Fashion and lifestyle magazine, Vogue, says 'building an excellent capsule wardrobe takes time and patience'.
sentences.chinese: 时尚生活杂志《VOGUE》称“打造一个优质的胶囊衣橱需要时间和耐心”。

sentences.chinese: 但如果你既想减少衣物浪费，又想在早上多睡几分钟，那现在或许就是开启胶囊衣橱计划的好时机！

title: Can we improve our memory
paragraphs: We've all been there – staring at a pile of books, desperately hoping that what we study will stick in our mind. Many of us have probably asked if there's any way that we can get better at remembering things. So, why don't we look at what memory experts say about this?

Every student who has made flashcards knows that it can be helpful to go back over what they've studied before. According to The Learning Scientists – a group of cognitive scientists – we can learn things better if we wait for some time before trying to study them again. They say that trying to retrieve something from your memory after you have had some time to forget it will make it easier to remember in future.

Similarly, David Robson, writing for BBC Future, highlights studies that show taking some time to just do nothing after studying might mean that you can remember things better afterwards. We don't know exactly why this happens, but it has been suggested that it's to do with the relationship between long-term and short-term memory.

Another study tip from The Learning Scientists is to change between different topics as you study. They say this can help you build links between different ideas. Now, linking ideas and relating them to each other or to images are often suggested as good ways to memorise something. Former world memory champion Jonathan Hancock highlights how picturing pieces of information in different physical locations or linking them to memorable images makes them easier to remember.

Linking new information to things that are easier to remember is a technique that many people use – it could be making letter patterns into words called mnemonics, or by sorting things into categories.

There are also more general things that we can do to improve our memory. Hancock says that being generally organised makes things easier for your brain, while many other experts also recommend avoiding stress, alcohol and smoking, and that we should get a lot of rest and exercise. So, the good news to take from this is that while it may be hard, improving our memory is something we can control.

vocabulary.translation: 这项研究聚焦于儿童幼儿时期的认知发展。
