title: Smarter ways to learn from failure
titleChinese: 从失败中学习的聪明方法
paragraphs: Many of us were told from an early age that, be it at school or in life, "you learn from your mistakes". But is this actually true?

The short answer is 'yes' – failure can be a teachable moment. But learning from our mistakes is, in reality, very hard because we don't like to fail. It doesn't feel good, so we react to failure in impulsive and emotional ways, like giving up on a task prematurely, telling ourselves we don't care whether we succeed, or finding fault with the task itself. This is self-protective, according to Hallgeir Sjåstad, a professor of psychology and leadership at the Norwegian School of Economics. "Most of us want to think of ourselves as competent and capable", he says, so when we fail "it poses a serious threat to our self-image".

Fortunately, there is research to suggest that there are some strategies to help us overcome the emotional barriers around failure. One of them is to adopt a third-person perspective. Instead of asking "Why did I fail?", we could ask "Why did Sam fail?", for example. Multiple studies by psychologist Ethan Kross at the University of Michigan show that adopting a third-person perspective helps to soften our negative emotional reactions, allowing us to look at failure more objectively.

A second strategy involves offering advice to others who may be in the same position as us. This strategy led to better levels of motivation and academic success in the test groups – involving both adults and children – that were asked to give advice based on their own failures. Professors Eskreis-Winkler, Fishbach and Duckworth found that the satisfaction of helping others "forces people to engage with their experience and what they have learned".

The writer Samuel Beckett once said: "fail again, fail better". But it now seems that we should be saying: "fail again, fail smarter". Failure is an inevitable part of life, but by learning to overcome the emotional barriers around it, we may find the road to success is a little easier to navigate.

vocabulary.entry: teachable moment /ˈtiːtʃəbl ˈməʊmənt/ 有教育意义的时刻；可从中学习的契机
vocabulary.example: Every difficult experience can be a teachable moment for personal growth.
vocabulary.translation: 每一次艰难的经历都能成为个人成长中一次可从中学习的契机。

vocabulary.entry: impulsive /ɪmˈpʌlsɪv/ adj. 冲动的；凭直觉行事的
vocabulary.example: She regretted her impulsive decision to quit the job without a plan.
vocabulary.translation: 她后悔自己一时冲动，没做任何计划就辞了职。

vocabulary.entry: prematurely /ˌpriːməˈtjʊəli/ adv. 过早地；仓促地
vocabulary.example: Don't judge the result prematurely before the project is completely finished.
vocabulary.translation: 在项目彻底完成前，不要过早地评判结果。

vocabulary.entry: find fault with /faɪnd fɔːlt wɪð/ 挑剔；找茬；对……吹毛求疵
vocabulary.example: He always finds fault with every detail instead of giving practical suggestions.
vocabulary.translation: 他总对每个细节吹毛求疵，却从不出具实际的建议。

vocabulary.entry: self-protective /ˌself prəˈtektɪv/ adj. 自我保护的
vocabulary.example: Her quiet attitude is a self-protective response to the hurt she suffered before.
vocabulary.translation: 她沉默的态度是对过往所受伤害的一种自我保护反应。

vocabulary.entry: psychology /saɪˈkɒlədʒi/ n. 心理学；心理状态
vocabulary.example: He studied psychology at university and now works as a professional counselor.
vocabulary.translation: 他大学主修心理学，如今是一名专业的心理咨询师。

vocabulary.entry: leadership /ˈliːdəʃɪp/ n. 领导力；领导才能
vocabulary.example: The company is looking for a manager with strong leadership and communication skills.
vocabulary.translation: 公司正在寻找一位兼具出色领导力和沟通能力的经理。

vocabulary.entry: competent /ˈkɒmpɪtənt/ adj. 有能力的；能胜任的；称职的
vocabulary.example: She is a competent teacher who can connect with students of all ages.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一位称职的老师，能和各个年龄段的学生建立良好沟通。

vocabulary.entry: capable /ˈkeɪpəbl/ adj. 有才能的；能干的；有能力做的
vocabulary.example: Anyone who is willing to learn is capable of mastering this basic skill.
vocabulary.translation: 任何愿意学习的人，都能掌握这项基础技能。

vocabulary.entry: pose /pəʊz/ v. 造成；带来（威胁、问题等）
vocabulary.example: This new policy could pose a potential threat to the development of small businesses.
vocabulary.translation: 这项新政策可能会给小企业的发展带来潜在威胁。

vocabulary.entry: self-image /ˌself ˈɪmɪdʒ/ n. 自我形象；自我认知
vocabulary.example: Constant criticism from others can easily damage a person's self-image.
vocabulary.translation: 他人的不断指责很容易损害一个人的自我形象。

vocabulary.entry: strategy /ˈstrætədʒi/ n. 策略；行动计划；方法
vocabulary.example: We need to develop a new marketing strategy to attract more young customers.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要制定新的营销策略，来吸引更多年轻消费者。

vocabulary.entry: overcome /ˌəʊvəˈkʌm/ v. 克服；战胜；攻克
vocabulary.example: She managed to overcome her fear of public speaking after months of practice.
vocabulary.translation: 经过数月的练习，她成功克服了对公开演讲的恐惧。

vocabulary.entry: emotional barrier /ɪˈməʊʃənl ˈbæriə(r)/ 情感障碍；情绪阻碍
vocabulary.example: Lack of trust has become the main emotional barrier between the two sides.
vocabulary.translation: 缺乏信任已经成为双方之间主要的情感障碍。

vocabulary.entry: adopt /əˈdɒpt/ v. 采用；采取；运用
vocabulary.example: The school decided to adopt a new teaching method to improve learning efficiency.
vocabulary.translation: 这所学校决定采用一种新的教学方法，来提升学习效率。

vocabulary.entry: third-person perspective /ˌθɜːd ˈpɜːsn pəˈspektɪv/ 第三人称视角
vocabulary.example: Looking at the problem from a third-person perspective helps you see the whole picture.
vocabulary.translation: 从第三人称视角看待问题，能帮你看清事情的全貌。

vocabulary.entry: soften /ˈsɒfn/ v. 缓和；减轻；使温和
vocabulary.example: A sincere apology can soften his anger and make communication possible again.
vocabulary.translation: 一句真诚的道歉能缓和他的怒气，让沟通重新成为可能。

vocabulary.entry: negative emotional reaction /ˈneɡətɪv ɪˈməʊʃənl riˈækʃn/ 负面情绪反应
vocabulary.example: Yelling and crying are common negative emotional reactions to frustration.
vocabulary.translation: 大喊和哭泣是面对挫败感时常见的负面情绪反应。

vocabulary.entry: objectively /əbˈdʒektɪvli/ adv. 客观地；不带偏见地
vocabulary.example: We need to analyze the data objectively instead of making subjective judgments.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要客观地分析数据，而非做出主观的判断。

vocabulary.entry: academic success /ˌækəˈdemɪk səkˈses/ 学业成功；学术成就
vocabulary.example: Hard work and effective learning methods are the keys to academic success.
vocabulary.translation: 努力付出和有效的学习方法，是学业成功的关键。

vocabulary.entry: test group /ˈtest ɡruːp/ 试验组；测试组
vocabulary.example: The test group showed significant improvement after using the new training method.
vocabulary.translation: 试验组在采用新的训练方法后，表现出了显著的进步。

vocabulary.entry: satisfaction /ˌsætɪsˈfækʃn/ n. 满足感；成就感；满意
vocabulary.example: She felt a great sense of satisfaction after finishing the challenging project.
vocabulary.translation: 完成这个具有挑战性的项目后，她感受到了强烈的成就感。

vocabulary.entry: engage with /ɪnˈɡeɪdʒ wɪð/ 深入思考；认真对待；参与
vocabulary.example: It's important to engage with your work if you want to achieve meaningful results.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你想取得有价值的成果，认真对待工作至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: inevitable /ɪnˈevɪtəbl/ adj. 不可避免的；必然发生的
vocabulary.example: Change is an inevitable part of life and we have to learn to adapt to it.
vocabulary.translation: 变化是生活中不可避免的一部分，我们必须学会去适应。

vocabulary.entry: navigate /ˈnævɪɡeɪt/ v. 顺利应对；处理；驾驭
vocabulary.example: She has the ability to navigate complex social situations with confidence and ease.
vocabulary.translation: 她有能力自信且从容地应对复杂的社交场合。

sentences.english: Many of us were told from an early age that, be it at school or in life, "you learn from your mistakes".
sentences.chinese: 我们很多人从小就被告知，无论是在学校还是生活中，“吃一堑，长一智”。

sentences.english: But is this actually true?
sentences.chinese: 但这话真的成立吗？

sentences.english: The short answer is 'yes' – failure can be a teachable moment.
sentences.chinese: 简短的答案是“是的”——失败可以成为一个具有教育意义的时刻。

sentences.english: But learning from our mistakes is, in reality, very hard because we don't like to fail.
sentences.chinese: 但事实上，从错误中学习并非易事，因为我们都不喜欢失败。

sentences.english: It doesn't feel good, so we react to failure in impulsive and emotional ways, like giving up on a task prematurely, telling ourselves we don't care whether we succeed, or finding fault with the task itself.
sentences.chinese: 失败的感觉并不好，所以我们会以冲动且情绪化的方式应对它，比如过早放弃一项任务、告诉自己不在乎成败，或是批评任务本身就有问题。

sentences.english: This is self-protective, according to Hallgeir Sjåstad, a professor of psychology and leadership at the Norwegian School of Economics.
sentences.chinese: 挪威经济学院心理学与领导力教授哈尔盖尔·肖斯塔德表示，这种反应是一种自我保护。

sentences.english: "Most of us want to think of ourselves as competent and capable", he says, so when we fail "it poses a serious threat to our self-image".
sentences.chinese: 他说：“我们大多数人都希望认为自己是有能力、能胜任的”，因此当我们失败时，“这会对我们的自我形象构成严重威胁”。

sentences.english: Fortunately, there is research to suggest that there are some strategies to help us overcome the emotional barriers around failure.
sentences.chinese: 幸运的是，有研究表明，存在一些策略可以帮助我们克服围绕失败产生的情绪障碍。

sentences.english: One of them is to adopt a third-person perspective.
sentences.chinese: 其中之一是采用第三人称视角。

sentences.english: Instead of asking "Why did I fail?", we could ask "Why did Sam fail?", for example.
sentences.chinese: 比如，不要问“我为什么失败了？”，而是问“山姆为什么失败了？”。

sentences.english: Multiple studies by psychologist Ethan Kross at the University of Michigan show that adopting a third-person perspective helps to soften our negative emotional reactions, allowing us to look at failure more objectively.
sentences.chinese: 密歇根大学心理学家伊桑·克罗斯开展的多项研究显示，采用第三人称视角有助于缓和我们的负面情绪反应，让我们能更客观地看待失败。

sentences.english: A second strategy involves offering advice to others who may be in the same position as us.
sentences.chinese: 第二种策略是为那些可能和我们处于相同境遇的人提供建议。

sentences.english: This strategy led to better levels of motivation and academic success in the test groups – involving both adults and children – that were asked to give advice based on their own failures.
sentences.chinese: 在一项涉及成人和儿童的测试中，那些被要求根据自己的失败经历给出建议的组别，展现出了更高的积极性和学业成就。

sentences.english: Professors Eskreis-Winkler, Fishbach and Duckworth found that the satisfaction of helping others "forces people to engage with their experience and what they have learned".
sentences.chinese: 埃斯克雷斯-温克勒、菲什巴赫和达克沃斯三位教授发现，帮助他人带来的满足感“会促使人们反思自己的经历以及从中收获的教训”。

sentences.english: The writer Samuel Beckett once said: "fail again, fail better".
sentences.chinese: 作家塞缪尔·贝克特曾说过：“再试一次，败得更漂亮些。”

sentences.english: But it now seems that we should be saying: "fail again, fail smarter".
sentences.chinese: 但现在我们似乎应该说：“再试一次，败得更明智些。”

sentences.english: Failure is an inevitable part of life, but by learning to overcome the emotional barriers around it, we may find the road to success is a little easier to navigate.
sentences.chinese: 失败是人生中不可避免的一部分，但通过学会克服其带来的情绪障碍，我们或许能让通往成功的道路变得更容易一些。

title: Sing for your health!
paragraphs: Whether you love to belt out tunes at karaoke or just sing in the shower, it turns out that singing can be good for both physical and mental health. And you don't even have to be good at it!

The physical and mental advantages of singing are caused by a combination of factors, according to Baishali Mukherjee from the World Federation of Music Therapy. He told BBC Future, "The physical exertion involved in singing – filling of our lungs, the firm control of our vocal cords, the movements of our mouth and body – is among the reasons why it can boost our mood." Hitting all the notes involves breathing control and the use of the diaphragm. This can lead to an increase of oxygen intake and lung capacity.

Also, apparently, singing in a group brings just as many benefits as singing solo. It has been estimated that over 2.2 million people in Britain now regularly sing in a choir. A choir can be amateur or professional and is made up of people who sing together, often in harmony with different people singing different parts, such as soprano or tenor, according to their vocal range.

A 2022 University of Vienna study found that choral singing enhances feelings of trust and bonding among a group, which can help with depression and loneliness. And, aside from mood-boosting, other proven mental health benefits of singing include a lowering of stress and anxiety levels due to the release of endorphins – the so-called "happy hormones".

So, whether you are a confident vocalist or not, give singing a go! You don't need an instrument because that's you. And yes, you might forget the lyrics or sound a little out of tune, but remember, there are a wealth of positives.

vocabulary.entry: belt out tunes /belt aʊt tjuːn/ 放声高歌；大声唱曲子
vocabulary.example: She likes to belt out tunes while she's cooking in the kitchen.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢在厨房做饭时放声高歌。

vocabulary.entry: karaoke /ˌkæriˈəʊki/ n. 卡拉OK；卡拉OK演唱
vocabulary.example: We booked a private room at the karaoke for my friend's birthday.
vocabulary.translation: 我们为朋友的生日在卡拉OK订了一个包间。

vocabulary.entry: combination /ˌkɒmbɪˈneɪʃn/ n. 结合；组合；混合因素
vocabulary.example: The team's success comes from a combination of hard work and good strategy.
vocabulary.translation: 这支队伍的成功源于努力和优秀策略的结合。

vocabulary.entry: music therapy /ˈmjuːzɪk ˈθerəpi/ 音乐疗法
vocabulary.example: Music therapy is used to help people cope with emotional and physical stress.
vocabulary.translation: 音乐疗法被用于帮助人们应对情绪和身体上的压力。

vocabulary.entry: physical exertion /ˈfɪzɪkl ɪɡˈzɜːʃn/ 体力消耗；身体活动量
vocabulary.example: This job requires a lot of physical exertion and not just mental work.
vocabulary.translation: 这份工作需要大量的体力付出，而不只是脑力劳动。

vocabulary.entry: lung /lʌŋ/ n. 肺；肺部
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise can help keep your lung in good condition.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动有助于保持肺部健康。

vocabulary.entry: vocal cord /ˈvəʊkl kɔːd/ n. 声带
vocabulary.example: Rest is important for a damaged vocal cord to heal properly.
vocabulary.translation: 声带受损后，休息对其正常恢复至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: boost /buːst/ v. 提升；促进；增强
vocabulary.example: A cup of tea can boost your energy when you feel tired.
vocabulary.translation: 感到疲惫时，一杯茶能为你补充精力。

vocabulary.entry: note /nəʊt/ n. 音符；音调；音高
vocabulary.example: He hit a high note at the end of the song that surprised everyone.
vocabulary.translation: 他在歌曲结尾唱出了一个高音，让所有人都感到意外。

vocabulary.entry: breathing control /ˈbriːðɪŋ kənˈtrəʊl/ 呼吸控制；调息
vocabulary.example: Breathing control is a basic skill that all singers need to learn.
vocabulary.translation: 呼吸控制是所有歌手都需要学习的基础技能。

vocabulary.entry: diaphragm /ˈdaɪəfræm/ n. 膈；横膈膜
vocabulary.example: Using the diaphragm correctly helps singers produce a stronger voice.
vocabulary.translation: 正确运用横膈膜能帮助歌手唱出更有力的声音。

vocabulary.entry: oxygen intake /ˈɒksɪdʒən ˈɪnteɪk/ 摄氧量；氧气吸入量
vocabulary.example: Deep breathing can increase your oxygen intake and calm your nerves.
vocabulary.translation: 深呼吸能提升你的摄氧量，平复情绪。

vocabulary.entry: lung capacity /ˈlʌŋ kəˈpæsəti/ 肺活量
vocabulary.example: Swimming is a great sport to improve your lung capacity.
vocabulary.translation: 游泳是提升肺活量的绝佳运动。

vocabulary.entry: solo /ˈsəʊləʊ/ adv. 独自地；单独地 n. 独唱；独奏
vocabulary.example: The musician played a piano solo that brought the audience to tears.
vocabulary.translation: 这位音乐家的钢琴独奏让观众热泪盈眶。

vocabulary.entry: choir /ˈkwaɪə(r)/ n. 合唱团；唱诗班
vocabulary.example: She joined the local choir to meet people who love singing.
vocabulary.translation: 她加入了当地的合唱团，结识志同道合的歌唱爱好者。

vocabulary.entry: amateur /ˈæmətə(r)/ adj. 业余的；非专业的 n. 业余爱好者
vocabulary.example: He is an amateur painter who paints in his free time.
vocabulary.translation: 他是一位业余画家，利用业余时间作画。

vocabulary.entry: harmony /ˈhɑːməni/ n. 和声；和谐；融洽
vocabulary.example: The four singers sang in perfect harmony during the performance.
vocabulary.translation: 四位歌手在演出中唱出了完美的和声。

vocabulary.entry: soprano /səˈprɑːnəʊ/ n. 女高音；女高音歌手 adj. 女高音的
vocabulary.example: The soprano has a clear voice that suits classical music perfectly.
vocabulary.translation: 这位女高音的嗓音清亮，十分适合演唱古典音乐。

vocabulary.entry: tenor /ˈtenə(r)/ n. 男高音；男高音歌手；音域
vocabulary.example: He has a natural tenor voice and was asked to join the choir.
vocabulary.translation: 他天生拥有男高音嗓音，被邀请加入了合唱团。

vocabulary.entry: vocal range /ˈvəʊkl reɪndʒ/ 音域；歌唱音域
vocabulary.example: Her wide vocal range allows her to sing both high and low songs.
vocabulary.translation: 她宽广的音域让她既能唱高音也能唱低音歌曲。

vocabulary.entry: choral singing /ˈkɔːrəl ˈsɪŋɪŋ/ 合唱；集体歌唱
vocabulary.example: Choral singing is a popular activity for people of all ages in this town.
vocabulary.translation: 合唱是这个小镇上各个年龄段的人都喜爱的活动。

vocabulary.entry: bonding /ˈbɒndɪŋ/ n. 建立亲密关系；情感联结
vocabulary.example: Shared activities are a great way to encourage bonding among team members.
vocabulary.translation: 共同的活动是促进团队成员间情感联结的好方法。

vocabulary.entry: endorphin /enˈdɔːfɪn/ n. 内啡肽
vocabulary.example: Laughing can trigger the release of endorphin in the human body.
vocabulary.translation: 大笑能促进人体内啡肽的分泌。

vocabulary.entry: vocalist /ˈvəʊkəlɪst/ n. 歌手；声乐表演者
vocabulary.example: The band is looking for a new vocalist with a unique singing style.
vocabulary.translation: 这支乐队正在寻找一位演唱风格独特的新歌手。

vocabulary.entry: lyric /ˈlɪrɪk/ n. 歌词；抒情诗 adj. 抒情的
vocabulary.example: I love this song because its lyric is full of warm feelings about home.
vocabulary.translation: 我喜欢这首歌，因为它的歌词充满了对家的温情。

vocabulary.entry: out of tune /aʊt ɒv tjuːn/ 走调；跑调；音调不准
vocabulary.example: He was so nervous that he sang out of tune at the start of the show.
vocabulary.translation: 他太紧张了，演出一开始就唱跑调了。

sentences.english: Whether you love to belt out tunes at karaoke or just sing in the shower, it turns out that singing can be good for both physical and mental health.
sentences.chinese: 不管你是喜欢在卡拉OK放声高歌，还是只爱在淋浴时哼上几句，事实证明，唱歌对身心健康都大有裨益。

sentences.english: And you don't even have to be good at it!
sentences.chinese: 而且你甚至不需要唱得有多好听！

sentences.english: The physical and mental advantages of singing are caused by a combination of factors, according to Baishali Mukherjee from the World Federation of Music Therapy.
sentences.chinese: 世界音乐治疗联合会的巴伊沙莉·慕克吉表示，唱歌带来的身心益处是多种因素共同作用的结果。

sentences.english: He told BBC Future, "The physical exertion involved in singing – filling of our lungs, the firm control of our vocal cords, the movements of our mouth and body – is among the reasons why it can boost our mood."
sentences.chinese: 他在接受BBC未来频道采访时说：“唱歌时的身体活动——充盈肺部、稳定控制声带、嘴巴和身体的协调动作——都是它能改善我们心情的原因之一。”

sentences.english: Hitting all the notes involves breathing control and the use of the diaphragm. This can lead to an increase of oxygen intake and lung capacity.
sentences.chinese: 唱准每一个音符需要控制呼吸并运用横膈膜，这会增加氧气摄入量，提升肺活量。

sentences.english: Also, apparently, singing in a group brings just as many benefits as singing solo.
sentences.chinese: 并且，似乎合唱和独唱带来的益处不相上下。

sentences.english: It has been estimated that over 2.2 million people in Britain now regularly sing in a choir.
sentences.chinese: 据估计，目前英国有超过220万人定期参加合唱团。

sentences.english: A choir can be amateur or professional and is made up of people who sing together, often in harmony with different people singing different parts, such as soprano or tenor, according to their vocal range.
sentences.chinese: 合唱团分业余和专业两种，由在一起唱歌的人组成，成员会根据自身音域分唱不同声部，比如女高音或男高音，从而演绎出和声效果。

sentences.english: A 2022 University of Vienna study found that choral singing enhances feelings of trust and bonding among a group, which can help with depression and loneliness.
sentences.chinese: 维也纳大学2022年的一项研究发现，合唱能增强群体成员之间的信任感和凝聚力，这有助于缓解抑郁和孤独感。

sentences.english: And, aside from mood-boosting, other proven mental health benefits of singing include a lowering of stress and anxiety levels due to the release of endorphins – the so-called "happy hormones".
sentences.chinese: 除了改善心情之外，唱歌对心理健康的其他经证实的益处还包括：唱歌会促使分泌内啡肽——即所谓的“快乐荷尔蒙”，从而降低压力和焦虑水平。

sentences.english: So, whether you are a confident vocalist or not, give singing a go!
sentences.chinese: 所以，无论对于唱歌是否自信，你都不妨试试！

sentences.english: You don't need an instrument because that's you.
sentences.chinese: 你不需要任何乐器，因为你自己就是乐器。

sentences.english: And yes, you might forget the lyrics or sound a little out of tune, but remember, there are a wealth of positives.
sentences.chinese: 没错，你可能会忘词，也可能会跑调，但请记住，唱歌带来的好处数不胜数。
